article_content: Louis Walsh has accepted €500,000 (£403,500) in libel damages from The Sun (Ireland) after the newspaper published a false story claiming he sexually assaulted a man in a Dublin nightclub. The out-of-court settlement follows a lawsuit filed by Walsh against News Group Newspapers over a June 23, 2011 article alleging he was under investigation for groping Leonard Watters, a 24-year-old unemployed dance teacher, after a Westlife concert in April 2011. Watters was later jailed for six months in July 2012 after being convicted of making a false report to An Garda Síochána, Ireland’s national police force. In court, Eoin McCullough, senior counsel for News Group Newspapers, issued a formal apology on behalf of The Sun, stating: 'The Sun fully accepts that the alleged assault did not occur and Louis Walsh is entirely innocent. We unreservedly apologize for the distress caused.' Walsh, accompanied by his legal team including solicitor Paul Tweed, described the ordeal as deeply traumatic. 'It was all lies,' he said outside court. 'I’m very relieved to be vindicated, but I remain angry at how The Sun treated me.' Tweed condemned the publication, calling it a 'prime example' of how unfounded allegations — amplified by the internet — can cause irreversible harm. He noted that while Watters has been criminally convicted, the damage from the global spread of the story could not be undone. Walsh emphasized that although no sum of money could fully compensate him, the settlement represented a definitive rejection of the falsehoods. He also expressed respect for most journalists but criticized The Sun for ignoring his denials and publishing the story without proper verification. His comments come ahead of the UK’s Leveson Report, which aimed to reform press standards following widespread media scandals.
translated_content: Kinabigyan ni Louis Walsh ang €500,000 (£403,500) bilang pinsala sa pagkakasala mula sa The Sun (Ireland) matapos na ipahayag ng pahayagan ang isang maling kuwento na nagmumungkahi na siya ay nagsagawa ng pang-aabuso sekswal sa isang lalaki sa isang nightclub sa Dublin. Ang kasunduang labas ng korte ay sumunod sa isang panukala na isinampa ni Walsh laban sa News Group Newspapers tungkol sa isang artikulo noong ika-23 ng Hunyo, 2011 na nagsasabi na siya ay pinag-aaralan sa paggaspang kay Leonard Watters, isang 24-taong-gulang na walang trabaho na guro ng sayaw, matapos ang isang konsiyerto ng Westlife noong Abril 2011. Ibinilanggo si Watters ng anim na buwan noong Hulyo 2012 matapos na mahatulan ng paggawa ng maling ulat sa An Garda Síochána, ang pambansang pulisya ng Ireland. Sa korte, ang Eoin McCullough, senior counsel para sa News Group Newspapers, ay naglabas ng pormal na paumanhin sa ngalan ng The Sun, na nagsasabi: 'Kabuuang tinatanggap ng The Sun na hindi nangyari ang nasabing pang-aabuso at si Louis Walsh ay ganap na walang kasalanan. Kami ay humihingi ng paumanhin nang walang pag-aalinlangan para sa kalungkutan na dulot ng aming artikulo.' Si Walsh, kasama ang kanyang koponang legal kabilang ang abogadong si Paul Tweed, ay ilarawan ang karanasan bilang malalim na traumatisado. 'Lahat ito ay mga kasinungalingan,' sabi niya sa labas ng korte. 'Napakagalak kong maging mapagpalaya, ngunit nananatiling galit ako sa paraan kung paano tinratuhan ako ng The Sun.' Sinugpo ni Tweed ang pagpapalabas, tinitingnan ito bilang 'isang pangunahing halimbawa' kung paano maaaring magdulot ng hindi maibabalik na pinsala ang mga maling akusasyon — na pinakalakas ng internet. Napansin niya na habang kinulong na si Watters dahil sa krimen, ang pinsala mula sa pandaigdigang pagkalat ng kuwento ay hindi maisasara. Pinahalagahan ni Walsh na kahit anong halaga ng pera ay hindi makakapagbayad sa kanyang ginawa, ngunit ang kasunduan ay kumakatawan sa isang tiyak na pagtanggol sa katotohanan. Ginawa rin niyang malinaw na may respeto siya sa karamihan sa mga journalist ngunit kritiko siya sa The Sun dahil sa pag-iwas sa kanyang pagtanggi at paglalathala ng kuwento nang walang sapat na pag-verify. Ang kanyang mga komento ay sumunod sa paglabas ng Leveson Report sa UK na layuning baguhin ang mga istandar ng media matapos ang mga napakalawak na skandal sa media.

article_content: Princeton, New Jersey (CNN) — In 2010, conservative columnist and CNN contributor David Frum sounded an alarm about the direction of his own party. Having served as a speechwriter for President George W. Bush, Frum feared that the Republican Party, emboldened by the Tea Party movement, was chasing short-term electoral victories at the expense of its long-term future. 'A party must champion the values of the voters it already has,' he wrote, 'but it must also speak to the votes it still needs to win.' After the 2008 election — a crushing defeat for Republicans following low approval ratings for Bush and John McCain’s loss — the Tea Party injected energy into the GOP base. Activists mobilized voters frustrated with the political establishment, pushing the party to prioritize deficit reduction and government spending cuts. They pressured congressional leaders to reject compromise, helping Republicans gain control of the House in the 2010 midterms and putting President Barack Obama on the defensive. But Frum’s warning proved prescient. The Tea Party’s influence exacted a heavy price. In 2010 and 2012, it helped defeat moderate Republican Senate candidates who were likely to win general elections — including Delaware’s Michael Castle, Nevada’s Sharron Angle, and Colorado’s Ken Buck. Each lost to Democrats. In 2012, veteran Senator Richard Lugar of Indiana fell to Tea Party-backed Richard Mourdock, whose controversial remarks on abortion sealed his defeat — and handed the seat to Democrat Joe Donnelly. The movement also crippled GOP negotiating power. During the 2011 fiscal cliff talks, hardline Tea Party members refused to support any deal involving tax increases, even as a last-minute compromise might have spared the country from automatic spending cuts. Their gamble — that voters would deliver a Republican president in 2012 — backfired. Obama won reelection, leaving Republicans with diminished leverage. Today, the GOP faces higher taxes and deeper defense cuts than it might have avoided. Even if a deal is reached, the public may view Obama as the decisive leader and Republicans as forced into concessions — a perception that further weakens the party’s image. Beyond policy, the Tea Party damaged the GOP’s attempt to rebrand as a party of governance rather than obstruction. Its insistence on ideological purity pushed leaders like House Speaker John Boehner and Senate Minority Leader Mitch McConnell to avoid compromise, reinforcing scholarly critiques from Thomas Mann and Norman Ornstein that the GOP has become dangerously polarized. The movement also alienated critical voting blocs. In 2012, the GOP lost nearly 70% of the Latino vote, partly due to hardline anti-immigration rhetoric amplified by Tea Party figures. Younger voters, too, found the party’s message unappealing. Voices like Bush’s, urging outreach to new demographics, were drowned out. As journalist Julian Zelizer notes, the Tea Party’s legacy is one of erosion — not empowerment. Frum recently asked: 'Have we learned our lesson yet?' The answer remains uncertain. With more traditionally red states trending purple, the GOP’s greatest threat may no longer come from Democrats — but from within.

Bush, kinabahan si Frum na ang Partido Republican, na pinagbigyan ng lakas ng kilosang Tea Party, ay naglalayong makamit ang maikling panahong pananakop sa eleksyon sa halip na mag-iingat sa pangmatagalang kinabukasan. Pagkatapos ng eleksyon noong 2008 — isang malaking pagkatalo para sa mga Republican pagkatapos ng mababang antas ng pagtanggap kay Bush at pagkatalo ni John McCain — ang Tea Party ay nagbigay ng buhay sa base ng GOP. Ang mga aktibista ay nagmobilisa sa mga botohan na nasaktan sa kalagayan ng pulitika, at pinaglalaban ang partido para sa pagbabawas ng depisyit at pagpapabawas sa gastos ng pamahalaan. Pinilit nila ang mga lider sa Kongreso na huwag makipagkasundo, at tumulong sa pagkakaroon ng kontrol ng Kapulungan ng mga Kinatawan ng mga Republican sa mga gitnang eleksyon noong 2010, at naglagay kay Pangulong Barack Obama sa posisyon ng depensa. Ngunit tinotoo ng babala ni Frum. Ang impluwensya ng Tea Party ay nagdulot ng malaking gastos. Noong 2010 at 2012, itinanggal nito ang ilang modera at kandidato ng Senado ng GOP na may malaking posibilidad na manalo sa pangkalahatang eleksyon — kasama na ang Michael Castle ng Delaware, Sharron Angle ng Nevada, at Ken Buck ng Colorado. Bawat isa ay natatalo ng mga Demokrata. Noong 2012, ang veteran na senador na si Richard Lugar ng Indiana ay napagtagisan ni Richard Mourdock, na ang kontrobersyal na pahayag tungkol sa aborsyon ang humantong sa kanyang pagkatalo — at ibinigay ang puwesto sa Demokrata na si Joe Donnelly. Ang kilusan ay nagpahirap din sa kakayahang mangnegosyo ng GOP. Noong mga pag-uusap sa 'fiscal cliff' noong 2011, ang mga miyembro ng Tea Party ay tumanggi na suportahan ang anumang kasunduan na may pagtaas ng buwis, kahit na ang isang kompromiso sa huling sandali ay maaaring maiwasan ang awtomatikong pagbawas sa gastos. Ang kanilang pagtaya — na ang mga botohan ay magdadala ng isang presidente na Republican noong 2012 — ay bumagsak. Nanalo si Obama, at nanatili ang mga Republican sa mas mababang lakas. Ngayon, kinakaharap ng GOP ang mas mataas na buwis at mas malalim na pagbawas sa depensa kaysa sa maaaring maiwasan. Kahit na makakamit ang isang kasunduan, maaaring tingnan ng publiko si Obama bilang desisyon at ang mga Republican bilang pilit na nagpasya — isang pananaw na nagpapahina pa sa imahe ng partido. Bukod sa patakaran, binasag ng Tea Party ang pagsubok ng GOP na maging partido ng pamamahala, hindi ng pagkakaantala. Ang pagtitiyak nito sa ideolohikal na kalinisan ay nagpilit sa mga lider tulad ng Speaker ng Kapulungan na si John Boehner at Minority Leader ng Senado na si Mitch McConnell na iwasan ang pagkakasundo, at nagpapalakas sa mga kritikal na pagsusuri mula kay Thomas Mann at Norman Ornstein na ang GOP ay naging masyadong polarizado. Ang kilusan ay nag-alienate rin sa mga mahalagang bloke ng botohan. Noong 2012, nawala ang GOP ng halos 70% ng boto ng Latino, parte dahil sa mga pahayag laban sa imigrasyon na pinapalakas ng mga miyembro ng Tea Party. Ang mga batang millennial, gayundin, ay nagsimulang mahanap na walang kasiyahan sa mensahe ng partido. Ang mga boses tulad ni Bush, na nagtataguyod ng pagpapalawak sa mga bagong grupo, ay nalunod. Ayon kay Julian Zelizer, ang taglay ng Tea Party ay isang pagkabigo — hindi pagpapalakas. Tanong ni Frum: 'Nakatutok na ba tayo sa aral?' Ang sagot ay hindi tiyak. Habang ang maraming tradisyonal na estado na pula ay nagsisilbing pula o kahit na maging palitan, ang pinakamalaking banta ng partido ay maaaring hindi mula sa mga Demokrata — kundi mula sa loob.

article_content: Experts are observing a noticeable slowdown in the UK housing market, driven by record-high prices and stricter mortgage regulations. Although the number of first-time buyers reaching out to estate agents increased last month, the pace of growth has slowed to its lowest level since February 2013. In London — where fears of a housing bubble are most intense — buyer inquiries declined for the first time since January last year. According to the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (RICS), potential purchasers are growing more cautious as affordability pressures mount and lending standards tighten. Estate agents now project London home prices will climb by just under 5% annually over the next five years, a significant drop from the 9% forecast just three months ago. This shift aligns London’s growth trajectory with the national average, easing pressure on the Bank of England to intervene. Simon Rubinsohn, RICS’s chief economist, noted that while the market remains broadly stable, the once-rapid upward momentum is fading, influenced by limited inventory, elevated prices, and clearer warnings from central bankers. New rules from the April Mortgage Market Review require lenders to conduct deeper affordability assessments, especially under rising interest rate scenarios. As a result, the average loan-to-value ratio for first-time buyers fell slightly from 86% in April to 85.3% in May. Meanwhile, the scarcity of homes for sale continues to discourage buyers. RICS now expects nationwide house prices to rise by only 3.6% over the next year — the weakest projection since December. Bank of England official Ben Broadbent, set to become deputy governor next month, warned that although mortgage debt is still low, rapid price gains could fuel risky lending, threatening financial stability. He emphasized that the Financial Policy Committee stands ready to act if credit growth becomes unsustainable. Recent data from Halifax showed homes in Britain rose by £223 per day in May — the largest daily jump in over 30 years — while ONS figures revealed London prices are now nearly 25% above their pre-recession peak. With the FPC’s next meeting looming, policymakers are under growing pressure to assess whether the market needs direct intervention to prevent a potential crisis.

Bagaman tumataas ang bilang ng mga unang-bahay na bumibili na nagkukontak sa mga estate agent noong nakaraang buwan, ang bilis ng pagtaas ay bumaba sa pinakamababang antas mula pa noong Pebrero 2013. Sa London — kung saan ang mga takot sa bubble ng tahanan ay pinakamatinding — bumaba ang mga tanong mula sa mga bagong mamimili para sa unang beses mula noong Enero taon nakalipas. Ayon sa Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (RICS), ang mga potensyal na mamimili ay nagiging mas maingat dahil sa pagtaas ng presyo at pagpapigil sa pagkakaloan. Ang mga estate agent ay nagtataya na tataas ang mga presyo ng bahay sa London ng halos 5% taun-taon sa susunod na limang taon, isang malaking pagbaba mula sa 9% na hinulaan lamang noong tatlong buwan ang nakalipas. Ang pagbabagong ito ay nagpapareho sa landas ng pag-unlad ng London sa pambansang average, na nagpapaliit sa presyon sa Bank of England upang magsagawa. Si Simon Rubinsohn, pangunahing ekonomista ng RICS, ay nagpaalala na habang nananatiling malakas ang merkado, ang dating mabilis na pagtaas ay nagsisimulang magbaba, naapektuhan ng kakulangan sa suplay, mataas na presyo, at mas malinaw na babala mula sa mga sentral na tagapagpaganap. Ang mga bagong patakaran mula sa Mortgage Market Review noong Abril ay nagsasailalim sa mga bangko na gawin ang mas detalyadong pagsusuri sa kakayahang magbayad, lalo na kung tataas ang mga rate ng interes. Bilang resulta, bumaba ang average na loan-to-value ratio para sa mga unang-bahay na mamimili mula sa 86% noong Abril hanggang 85.3% noong Mayo. Samantala, ang kakulangan sa mga bahay na nakalikha ay patuloy na nagpapababa sa interes ng mga mamimili. Ngayon ay inaasahan ng RICS na tataas ang mga presyo ng tahanan sa buong bansa ng 3.6% lamang sa susunod na taon — ang pinakamababang propesyonal na hula mula pa noong Disyembre. Ang opisyales ng Bank of England, si Ben Broadbent, na darating bilang pangalawang gobernador bukas, ay nagbanta na bagaman mababa pa rin ang utang sa mortgage, ang mabilis na pagtaas ng presyo ay maaaring magdulot ng riskier na pagkakaloan, na nagdudulot ng panganib sa pampublikong kaligtasan. Pinagtibay niya na handa ang Financial Policy Committee na magsagawa kung ang paglago ng kreditong ito ay magiging hindi mapanatili. Ang kamakailang datos mula sa Halifax ay ipinakita na tumataas ang presyo ng mga bahay sa Britain ng £223 araw-araw noong Mayo — ang pinakamalaking pagtaas sa araw-araw sa loob ng higit sa 30 taon — samantalang ang mga datos mula sa Office for National Statistics ay nagpapakita na ang mga presyo sa London ay halos 25% mas mataas kaysa sa kanilang peak bago ang recession. Habang dumadaan ang susunod na pagpupulong ng FPC, ang mga papolitika ay nasa mas malaking presyon upang suriin kung kailangan ng merkado ng direkta na pagtutok upang maiwasan ang posibleng krisis.

article_content: Celtic extended their push for the Scottish Premiership title with a convincing 2-0 triumph over Hamilton at New Douglas Park, in front of a stadium-record crowd of 6,007 fans. The visitors controlled the game from the outset, with Adam Matthews opening the scoring in the 33rd minute — his first goal for the club since August 2013. Picking up a precise pass from Kris Commons, Matthews unleashed a powerful, first-time shot from just inside the box that flew past goalkeeper Michael McGovern. Five minutes into the second half, Liam Henderson sealed the result with a low, driven finish from close range, marking his first goal since March. Despite Hamilton’s improved form following a winter training camp in Gran Canaria and a recent 2-0 win over Kilmarnock, they struggled to create consistent threats. Their best chance came late in the first half when a scrambled set-piece led to two frantic close-range efforts, both denied by Celtic keeper Craig Gordon. Captain Scott Brown, playing with a head bandage after sustaining a cut, led by example, while new additions Jason Denayer and Leigh Griffiths added steel and firepower to the midfield and attack. Though Hamilton’s Martin Canning returned to the backline after sitting out their midweek loss, the hosts rarely looked like threatening a comeback. Celtic remained composed under pressure, with Griffiths forcing another brilliant save from McGovern in the 76th minute, underscoring their dominance. The result ended any hope of Hamilton repeating their historic 1-0 win over Celtic from earlier in the season.

Ang mga bisita ay kontrolado ang laro mula sa simula, na may nagbubukas na goal ni Adam Matthews sa ika-33 minuto — ang kanyang unang goal para sa klub mula pa noong Agosto 2013. Pagkatanggap ng isang malinaw na pasalubong mula kay Kris Commons, sinabog ni Matthews ang isang makapangyarihang, direkta na hagis mula sa loob ng kahon na tumama sa gatekeeper na si Michael McGovern. Limang minuto lamang pagsapit ng ikalawang kalahati, siniguro ni Liam Henderson ang resulta sa pamamagitan ng isang mabilis na hagis mula sa malapit na saklaw, ang kanyang unang goal mula noong Marso. Sa kabila ng pagbabago ng anyo ng Hamilton pagkatapos ng isang winter training camp sa Gran Canaria at isang bagong 2-0 na panalo laban kay Kilmarnock, nahihirapan silang lumikha ng malinaw na mga banta. Ang pinakamalakas na pagkakataon nila ay nangyari sa huling bahagi ng una kalahati nang magkaroon ng isang nakakalito na set-piece na nagresulta sa dalawang malapit na hagis, pareho ay tinigil ni Celtic keeper na si Craig Gordon. Ang kapitan na si Scott Brown, na naglalaro habang may head bandage dahil sa sugat, ay nagbigay ng halimbawa, samantalang ang mga bagong kapalit na si Jason Denayer at Leigh Griffiths ay nagdagdag ng lakas at lakas sa gitna at serbisyo. Bagaman bumalik si Martin Canning ng Hamilton sa backline pagkatapos umalis sa kanilang midweek loss, hindi sila nagpakita ng kahit anumang seryosong banta sa pagtatapos. Nanatiling maayos ang Celtic sa ilalim ng presyon, na may nagpapakita ng isang malakas na hagis ni Griffiths kay McGovern sa ika-76 minuto, na nagpapakita ng kanilang dominasyon. article_content: Before you walked in, I took down all my Ted Cruz posters,' Carrie Brownstein says dryly, propped against the doorway of her Portland home. The line lands like a punchline — because everyone who knows her understands it’s pure irony. At 39, Brownstein isn’t just a musician turned actress; she’s become the face of a cultural archetype she both embodies and gently mocks. As co-creator and star of the IFC sketch comedy series 'Portlandia', she and Fred Armisen turn everyday quirks — like obsessive recycling rules or handcrafted bird-decorated goods — into hilarious, hyper-observant vignettes. Though the show is set in Portland and has made Brownstein a local icon, she insists it’s not really about the city. 'It’s about a mindset,' she explains. 'People who crave uniqueness — the feeling that something was made just for them. And yeah, I’m totally guilty of that too.' Her own 1912 bungalow in Grant Park tells the same story. Ten years after buying it, she’s filled it with relics of her passions: a taxidermied weasel once owned by Amy Sedaris, vintage Pacific Northwest paintings, and a staggering vinyl collection — thousands of records, alphabetized by artist, down to the last LP. These aren’t props. They’re proof that the line between performer and performance is thin. Even her personal life echoes the show. When she’s shooting for ELLE, Armisen — her longtime friend and collaborator since a 2003 SNL after-party — texts her to share the news of Lou Reed’s passing. He lives nearby during filming, often jamming in her basement studio, where five guitars lean against a Chesterfield sofa. But there’s a twist: the satire has seeped into her daily life. The 'Put a Bird on It' sketch — which lampoons artisans who plaster birds onto everything — now haunts her shopping trips. 'I’ll see a beautiful dress with birds on it,' she admits, 'and I just can’t bring myself to buy it. I feel like I’m endorsing the joke.' In other words, the mirror she holds up to hipster culture has reflected back something uncomfortably familiar.
translated_content: 'Bago kang pumasok, tinanggal ko lahat ng mga poster ni Ted Cruz,' sabi ni Carrie Brownstein nang walang emosyon, nakalek sa frame ng pinto ng kanyang silid-kainan sa Portland. Ang pangungusap ay mukhang isang joke — dahil alam ng lahat na kilala siya na ito ay puno ng tawa. Sa edad na 39, hindi lang si Brownstein isang musikero na naging aktres; naging simbolo na rin siya ng isang kultura na pinagsasama niya ang pagiging totoo at pagtatawa. Kasama ni Fred Armisen, isa siya sa mga tagapaglikha at bida ng komedyang sketch na 'Portlandia' sa IFC, kung saan sila ay nagpapakita ng mga simpleng gawi — tulad ng sobrang pagpapahalaga sa recycling o paglalagay ng mga larawan ng ibon sa mga bagay — bilang makabuluhang, mapagmasid na mga eksena. Bagaman ang palabas ay nangyayari sa Portland at ginawa siyang bayani sa lungsod, sinasabi niya na hindi ito tungkol sa lugar. 'Tungkol ito sa isang paraan ng pag-iisip,' sabi niya. 'Mga tao na gustong makaramdam na espesyal — na naniniwala na ang isang bagay ay gawa para lamang sa kanila. At oo, ako mismo ay may kasalanan din dito.' Ang kanyang sariling bahay na gawa noong 1912 sa Grant Park ay nagpapatotoo sa parehong kuwento. Sampung taon mula nang bumili, puno na ito ng mga bagay na may kinalaman sa kanyang mga pasyon: isang weasel na naitaas na dating ari ni Amy Sedaris, mga larawan ng kagandahan ng Pacific Northwest mula sa mga lokal na artista, at isang napakalaking koleksyon ng mga record — libo-libong vinyl, nakakabit sa alpabeto batay sa artista, hanggang sa huling LP. Hindi ito mga prop. Ito ay patotoo na malapit ang linya sa pagitan ng artista at papel na ginagampanan. Kahit sa kanyang personal na buhay, sumusunod siya sa palabas. Habang nagpapakita siya para sa ELLE, tinext ni Armisen — ang kanyang matagal nang kaibigan at kasamang musiko mula sa isang after-party ng SNL noong 2003 — upang ipaabot ang balita tungkol sa kamatayan ni Lou Reed. Naninirahan siya malapit habang nagpapakita, at madalas siyang tumatakas sa ilalim ng kanyang basement studio, kung saan limang gitara ang nakadikit sa isang Chesterfield sofa. Ngunit may isang pagbabago: ang pagtatawa ay naging bahagi na ng kanyang pang-araw-araw na buhay. Ang sketch na 'Put a Bird on It' — na pinagtatawanan ang mga artesano na naglalagay ng ibon sa lahat ng bagay — ay naging parusa sa kanyang mga pagbili. 'Makikita ko ang isang magandang damit na may mga ibon,' sabi niya, 'at hindi ko na kaya bumili. Parang tinutulungan ko ang joke.' Sa madaling salita, ang salamin na inilalabas niya sa kultura ng hipster ay nagbabalik sa kanya ng isang bagay na kakaibang pamilyar.

article_content: Asian stocks retreated from a two-and-a-half-month high on Wednesday as investors scaled back their earlier enthusiasm over the likelihood of an imminent end to U.S. interest rate hikes. The dollar, meanwhile, found support after recent losses. MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares excluding Japan had risen more than 3% over the past week and reached its highest level since September on Tuesday. However, it slipped 0.2% in early trading on Wednesday. Japan’s Nikkei advanced 0.5%, while the S&P 500 ended a five-session winning streak with a 0.2% decline. Chipmaker Nvidia reported revenue well above Wall Street forecasts after market close, yet its shares fell 1.7% due to a pessimistic outlook for sales in China. Nasdaq and S&P 500 futures both edged down by 0.1–0.2% in early Asian trading. Trading volumes are expected to remain subdued through the remainder of the week due to the upcoming Thanksgiving holiday in the United States. 'It appears the short-covering rally that began after the November Fed meeting is losing steam, with buying and selling now alternating,' said Naka Matsuzawa, Chief Macro Strategist at Nomura. Although the Federal Reserve released minutes from its November meeting overnight, traders viewed its pledge to 'proceed carefully' as largely consistent with prior messaging. Ten-year U.S. Treasury yields dipped slightly to 4.40% in Asian trade, having fallen roughly 50 basis points since the Fed held rates steady earlier in November. Markets now assign nearly zero probability to another Fed rate hike, pricing in approximately 90 basis points of cuts by the end of 2024—with a 30% chance the first reduction could come as early as March. 'Given the Fed’s belief that a soft landing is within reach, it would be unwise to jeopardize it with unnecessary hikes,' said Philip Marey, Senior U.S. Strategist at Rabobank. 'If stronger economic or inflation data emerges before the December meeting, long-term yields may rise instead—effectively substituting for a rate hike. We do not anticipate further increases.' In foreign exchange markets, the U.S. dollar stabilized after weakening following last week’s softer-than-expected U.S. inflation report. 'As U.S. inflation continues to moderate, yield differentials are likely to remain supportive for the yen and renminbi,' said Jonathan Petersen, Senior Economist at Capital Economics. China’s yuan, which has strengthened 2% against the dollar over the past week, steadied at 7.1356 in onshore trading. According to two sources familiar with the matter, China’s major state-owned banks have been purchasing yuan recently to accelerate its recovery. On the data front, Singapore’s economy grew faster than initially estimated in the third quarter, buoyed by a rebound in tourism. Later Wednesday, Reserve Bank of Australia Governor Michele Bullock is scheduled to speak, and U.S. jobless claims will be released. In commodities, Brent crude futures held just above their 50-day moving average at $82.64 per barrel. Singapore iron ore futures, up more than 10% for the month, traded at $131 per tonne. Bitcoin slipped to $36,163 after Binance CEO Changpeng Zhao stepped down and pleaded guilty to violating U.S. anti-money laundering laws as part of a $4.3 billion settlement resolving a years-long investigation. Meanwhile, India’s IPO market is experiencing a surge: three of the four offerings that opened Wednesday—Tata Technologies, Flair Writing Industries, and Gandhar Oil Refinery—were fully subscribed within hours. Separately, IndiGo plans to introduce a premium cabin class with hot meals and a loyalty program by the end of 2024 to better compete with Air India on international routes.

article_content: After a disappointing season-opening loss to the Boston Celtics, the Miami Heat bounced back with a 98-87 victory over the Philadelphia 76ers — their first win of the NBA season. LeBron James, Dwayne Wade, and Chris Bosh, collectively known as 'The Big Three,' finally tasted success together on the court, combining for 61 points. Wade led the charge with 30, followed by James with 16 and Bosh with 15. But the real surprise came from role player James Jones, who exploded for 20 points on just nine shots, earning effusive praise from his superstar teammates. 'JJ was unbelievable today,' James said. Wade echoed: 'Give it up for JJ — he really stepped up.' Coach Erik Spoelstra noted a clear shift in the team’s energy, especially on defense, saying they focused on keeping opponents in front and contesting every shot at the rim. Still, Wade cautioned that Miami isn’t anywhere near their best yet. 'We’re not even close,' he admitted, pointing to a shaky fourth quarter where the 76ers nearly tied the game. Meanwhile, the Celtics, who had celebrated their win over Miami, suffered a shocking 95-87 defeat to the Cleveland Cavaliers. This marked Cleveland’s first game without LeBron James since his dramatic July departure. Despite leading by 11 points in the third quarter, Boston collapsed in the final frame, getting outscored 27-14. Antawn Jamison and Daniel Gibson led the Cavs’ rally, with Gibson scoring all 16 of his points in the second half. Former Cavalier Shaquille O’Neal admitted Boston underestimated their former teammate’s squad. 'We took them a little too lightly,' he said. Elsewhere, the Knicks beat the Raptors 98-93, the Thunder topped the Bulls 106-95, and the Nets edged the Pistons 101-98 in tight Eastern Conference matchups.

article_content: Far too many passengers are being stranded on board commercial flights in the United States during delays, according to an air passengers' rights group. Delta Air Lines, JetBlue, Continental Airlines, and US Airways received an overall grade of 'F' on the air travel consumer report card released by FlyersRights.org. In 2008, there were more than 1,200 incidents of tarmac strandings — situations where passengers are confined on planes parked on runways. Delta Air Lines recorded the highest number of tarmac delays exceeding three hours. Southwest Airlines was rated the best for managing delays, allowing passengers to deplane and providing food, water, and other essentials. The longest reported delay occurred in January 2008 on a Delta flight from Atlanta, Georgia, to Florida, where passengers waited over 10 hours without food or water. 'Too many Americans have been locked inside sealed airplanes, trapped on the tarmac for three hours or more,' said Kate Hanni, Executive Director of FlyersRights.org. 'It's time for Congress to give airline passengers the legal right to get off planes stuck on the ground for three hours or more.' Hanni, who has been lobbying for an airline passengers' bill of rights, noted that economic pressures have worsened conditions: layoffs have led airlines to reduce services to protect profits. 'A timely flight is not just a matter of passenger convenience — it's a matter of public safety,' she added. 'I wonder if heroic Captain Chesley 'Sully' Sullenberger and his crew could have performed as they did after seven, nine, or even 12 hours on the tarmac?' Hanni founded FlyersRights.org after being stranded for over nine hours on an American Airlines flight in Austin, Texas, in December 2006. Mark Mogel, the group’s research director, said FlyersRights.org has approximately 24,000 members, many of whom contribute financially and through lobbying efforts. The report card is based on government data, press reports, airline websites, hotline submissions, and eyewitness accounts from January to December 2008. It evaluated 17 airlines across multiple criteria: frequency and duration of tarmac delays, meal provisions, and customer service policies, assigning individual scores and an overall grade. For meal provisions, the assessment focused on availability, not quality. Delta, JetBlue, Continental, and US Airways received an 'F'; American Airlines received a 'D'. United, AirTran, and American Eagle earned a 'C'. Alaska, Northwest, and Frontier received a 'B'. Southwest received an 'A'. Five airlines — Atlantic Southeast, Comair, ExpressJet, Mesa, and Pinnacle — were not graded due to incomplete data. The report’s executive summary stated: 'The fact that some airlines have received A's and B's while others received D's and F's shows that providing decent customer service and avoiding strandings is achievable and should not place an undue burden on the airline industry or lead to higher ticket prices.' CNN's Joe Sterling contributed to this report.

article_content: Beijing (CNN) — Diplomatic efforts to resolve the Chen Guangcheng case showed promising signs on Friday, as China indicated the activist could apply to travel to the United States, and New York University announced it had invited him to serve as a visiting scholar. China had been angered after Chen, who escaped house arrest, sought refuge at the U.S. Embassy in Beijing. After six days, he left the embassy and was taken to a hospital, where he was reunited with his wife and two children. Since then, Chen has repeatedly requested permission to leave China, including during a call to a U.S. congressional hearing. China’s willingness to permit his overseas travel was viewed as a significant step forward in resolving a tense and controversial standoff. "As a Chinese citizen, he may apply like any other Chinese citizen, following the laws and standard procedures of the relevant authorities," said Liu Weimin, a spokesperson for the Chinese Foreign Ministry. U.S. Secretary of State Hillary Clinton said Washington was "encouraged" by the statement. "From the beginning, all our actions regarding Mr. Chen have been guided by his choices and our shared values," she told reporters in Beijing. "Our ambassador spoke with him again today, and embassy staff and a physician met with him. He confirmed that he and his family wish to travel to the United States to pursue his studies." New York University confirmed it had invited Chen, 40, to join its law programs as a visiting scholar, noting his long-standing relationships with faculty. He would be based in New York or one of NYU’s global campuses. State Department spokeswoman Victoria Nuland said Chen had been offered a fellowship by an American university, with his wife and children permitted to accompany him. "The Chinese government has indicated it will accept Mr. Chen’s applications for appropriate travel documents," Nuland said. "The United States expects China to process these applications promptly and accommodate his medical needs. U.S. authorities will prioritize visa requests for him and his immediate family." U.S. Ambassador Gary Locke, who spoke with Chen by phone for 20 minutes, said Chen expressed his desire to study in the United States. Senior U.S. officials noted that as long as Chen had a legitimate academic offer and genuine intent to study, he would receive a student visa. "We believe these steps will unfold expeditiously," one official said. The fact that U.S. embassy staff and a doctor were able to meet Chen at the hospital underscored progress in the case. Earlier, Chen had reported that Chinese security personnel blocked U.S. diplomats from entering his room on Thursday. He is receiving treatment for a foot injury sustained during his escape. Friday marked the 10th birthday of Chen’s son; embassy staff brought him gifts. Clinton’s planned visit to Beijing for strategic and economic talks became dominated by negotiations over Chen’s case — a diplomatic flashpoint occurring just months before the U.S. presidential election and China’s once-in-a-decade leadership transition. Republican critics accused the Obama administration of being too soft on authoritarian regimes. Meanwhile, Chen participated remotely in a congressional hearing chaired by Republican Rep. Chris Smith of New Jersey. "China pledged to guarantee my constitutional rights and called me a free man," Chen said via speakerphone from his hospital room. "I want them to honor that commitment by allowing me to travel abroad to recover. I haven’t had a Sunday off in seven years. I want to go to the United States and rest." U.S. officials also met with Chen’s wife, Yuan Weijing, according to a senior State Department source. Chen expressed concern for relatives in Shandong Province, where he said authorities installed seven surveillance cameras, stationed guards, and planned to build an electric fence around his home. "They even laughed, ‘Let’s see what this blind man can do to us,’" he recounted. Despite earlier expressions of disappointment, Chen on Friday expressed deep gratitude to U.S. officials for their treatment during his time at the embassy. Jerome Cohen, an American law professor and Chen’s advisor, explained that Chen’s emotional state shifted after leaving the embassy. "Everything changed when he got to the hospital," Cohen said. "The U.S. team, exhausted, went home to rest. Chen was left alone — overwhelmed and vulnerable." Human rights advocates remain wary. Several of Chen’s associates have been detained or gone missing. He Peirong, the activist who first revealed Chen’s escape to CNN, reappeared Friday after being absent for a week. She confirmed she was safe but declined to elaborate. ChinaAid, a Texas-based Christian human rights group, criticized the dual message from Beijing: "Beijing gives Chen freedom with one hand and beats rights defenders with the other," said president Bob Fu. CNN contributors Jill Dougherty, Jaime FlorCruz, Steven Jiang, Dan Lothian, Eunice Yoon, Jethro Mullen, and Stan Grant contributed to this report.

Nagalit ang China pagkatapos tumakas si Chen mula sa bahay-arrest at humingi ng tulong sa U.S. Embassy sa Beijing. Pagkatapos ng anim na araw, umalis siya sa embahada at dinala sa ospital, kung saan muli niyang nakita ang asawa at dalawang anak niya. Mula noon, paulit-ulit niyang hiningi ang pahintulot na lumabas sa China, kabilang ang isang tawag sa isang pagpupulong sa Kongreso ng Estados Unidos. Ang pagtanggap ng China na payagan ang kanyang paglalakbay sa ibang bansa ay itinuring bilang isang malaking hakbang patungo sa paglutas ng isang tensyon at kontrobersyal na pagkakaiba-iba. "Bilang isang mamamayan ng Tsina, maaari siyang humiling tulad ng anumang ibang mamamayan ng Tsina, sumusunod sa mga batas at karaniwang proseso ng mga kaugnay na ahensya," sabi ni Liu Weimin, isang tagapagsalita ng Kansiyer para sa Panlabas na Ugnayang Tsino. Ang Sekretarya ng Estado ng Estados Unidos, Hillary Clinton, ay nagsabi na ang Washington ay "nagmamalaki" sa pahayag na iyon. "Mula sa simula, ang lahat ng aming aksyon tungkol kay Mr. Chen ay pinangunahan ng kanyang mga desisyon at aming mga halaga," sabi niya sa mga reporter sa Beijing. "Umulit na nagsalita ang aming ambasador sa kanya ngayon, at nakipagkita ang mga tauhan ng embahada at isang doktor. Kumpirmado niya na gusto niya at ng kanyang pamilya na umalis sa Estados Unidos upang matapos ang kanyang pag-aaral." Ipinatotoo ng New York University na binigyan si Chen, 40, ng panawagan na sumali sa mga programa sa batas nito bilang bisiting scholar, at sinabi nila ang kanyang mahabang ugnayan sa mga propesor. Sasakyan siya sa New York o sa isa sa mga pandaigdigang campus ng NYU. Ang tagapagsalita ng Kagawaran ng Estado, Victoria Nuland, ay nagsabi na binigyan si Chen ng isang stipendyo mula sa isang Amerikanong unibersidad, na may kakayahan na sundan siya ng asawa at mga anak niya. "Ipinaliwanag ng pamahalaang Tsino na tatanggapin nila ang mga aplikasyon ni Mr. Chen para sa mga angkop na dokumento sa paglalakbay," sabi ni Nuland. "Inaasahan ng pamahalaang Estados Unidos na mabilis na prosesuhin ng pamahalaang Tsino ang mga aplikasyon na ito at bigyan ng pansin ang kanyang medikal na kalagayan. Magbibigay ng prioridad ang pamahalaang Estados Unidos sa mga kahilingan sa visa para sa kanya at sa kanyang pamilya." Ang Ambasador ng Estados Unidos, Gary Locke, na nagsalita sa telepono kay Chen ng 20 minuto, ay nagsabi na ipinahayag ni Chen ang kanyang hangarin na mag-aral sa Estados Unidos. Ang mga opisyales ng Estados Unidos ay nagpaliwanag na habang may legitimo at serioyang tawag mula sa isang akreditadong institusyon, mabibigyan siya ng student visa. "Naniniwala kami na magkakaroon ng mabilis na pag-unlad ang mga hakbang na ito," sabi ng isang opisyales ng Estados Unidos. Ang katotohanan na nakakita ang mga tauhan ng embahada at isang doktor kay Chen sa ospital ay nagpapakita ng pag-unlad sa kaso. Nanguna pa noon, sinabi ni Chen na binitawan siya ng mga tauhan ng seguridad ng Tsina mula sa pagpasok sa kanyang silid sa ospital noong Huwebes. Kasalukuyang tinatanggap niya ang paggamot para sa sugat sa paa na nakuha niya habang tumakas. Noong Biyernes ay ika-10 kaarawan ng anak ni Chen; dinala ng mga tauhan ng embahada ang regalo para sa kanya. Ang plano ng pagbisita ni Clinton sa Beijing para sa mga talakayan sa estratehiko at ekonomiya ay naging sentro ng mga negosasyon tungkol sa kaso ni Chen — isang diplomaticong suliranin na naganap lamang ilang buwan bago ang eleksyon sa Estados Unidos at ang pagbabago sa liderato ng Tsina na mangyayari bawat sampung taon. Sinupil ng mga republikano ang administrasyon ni Obama dahil sa sobrang pagiging malambot sa mga rehimeng autoritaryo. Samantalang, sumali si Chen sa isang pagpupulong sa Kongreso na pinangunahan ni Rep. Chris Smith ng New Jersey. "Pinangako ng Tsina na pangalagaan ang aking mga karapatan ayon sa konstitusyon at tawagin ako bilang isang malayang tao," sabi ni Chen sa pamamagitan ng speakerphone mula sa kanyang silid sa ospital. "Gusto kong igawad nila ang kanilang pangako sa pamamagitan ng pagpapahintulot sa akin na lumabas sa bansa upang makarekuper. Hindi ako nakakapagpahinga sa Linggo sa loob ng pitong taon. Gusto kong umalis sa Estados Unidos at magpahinga." Kasama rin ang mga opisyales ng Estados Unidos ang asawa ni Chen, si Yuan Weijing, ayon sa isang senior opisyales ng Kagawaran ng Estado na hindi nais maitalang pangalan dahil sa sensitibidad ng usaping ito. Inirereklamo ni Chen ang kanyang mga kamag-anak sa lalawigan ng Shandong, kung saan sinabi niya na itinayo ng mga awtoridad ang pitong camera ng pagsubaybay, ipinapanatili ang mga guard, at inihanda ang pagtatayo ng elektrikong pader sa paligid ng kanyang bahay. "Kahit na tinawag nila, ‘Tingnan natin ano ang kayang gawin ng isang bulag na tao sa amin,’" sabi niya. Bagaman may nakaraang pagpapahayag ng pagkabigo, ipinahayag ni Chen noong Biyernes ang malalim na pasasalamat sa mga opisyales ng Estados Unidos para sa kanilang pagtrato sa kanya habang nasa embahada. Si Jerome Cohen, isang Amerikanong propesor sa batas at tagapayo ni Chen, ay nagbigay ng paliwanag kung bakit nabago ang emosyonal na kalagayan ni Chen pagkatapos umalis sa embahada. "Nabago lahat nang dumating siya sa ospital," sabi ni Cohen. "Ang lahat ng mga tao na gumawa ng maraming gawain upang siguraduhin ang kanyang kinabukasan mula sa embahada at Kagawaran ng Estado, ay naiwan na para magpahinga." Ang mga tagapagtanggol ng karapatang pantao ay nananatiling mapanuri. Maraming kasamahan ni Chen ang napapailalim sa pagkakakulong o nawawala. Si He Peirong, ang aktibista na una ring ipinahayag ang pagtakas ni Chen sa CNN, ay bumalik noong Biyernes pagkatapos ng isang linggong pagkawala. Kumpirmado niya na nasa kalinisan siya ngunit tumangging magbigay ng karagdagang komento. Ang ChinaAid, isang Texas-based Kristiyanong grupo para sa karapatang pantao, ay kritiko sa dual na mensahe mula sa Beijing: "Binibigyan ng kalayaan ni Beijing si Chen sa isang kamay at inaapi ang mga tagapagtanggol ng karapatan sa isa pang kamay," sabi ni Bob Fu, ang pangulo ng ChinaAid. Ang mga kontribyutor ng CNN na si Jill Dougherty, Jaime FlorCruz, Steven Jiang, Dan Lothian, Eunice Yoon, Jethro Mullen, at Stan Grant ay nakatulong sa ulat na ito.

article_content: When it comes to genetically modified foods, astrophysicist Neil deGrasse Tyson has a simple message: relax. In a recent video, he challenged the panic surrounding GMOs by pointing out that nearly everything we eat has already been changed by humans over thousands of years. Wild watermelons? Tiny and bitter. Wild cows? Don’t exist — we bred them. Every apple, banana, or potato on your grocery shelf is the product of deliberate breeding, long before labs existed. Tyson argues that today’s gene-editing techniques are just the next step in a practice as old as farming itself — artificial selection. Why, he asks, should we suddenly object when the tool moves from fields to test tubes? He urges critics to try eating a wild apple — sour, hard, and full of seeds — if they really want ‘natural’ food. Meanwhile, scientists are using modern biotechnology to tackle real-world crises. In Uganda, researchers are growing bananas enriched with pro-vitamin A to combat blindness and death from deficiency, a problem affecting hundreds of thousands of children annually in Africa. These ‘super bananas’ aren’t just science fiction — their flesh turns orange as nutrient levels rise, and clinical trials are set to begin soon. Major scientific bodies, including the National Academy of Sciences and the European Commission, agree: GMOs are not inherently dangerous. The real issue isn’t the technology — it’s whether we use it wisely, equitably, and transparently.

Mga wild cows? Wala sila — binago natin sila. Ang bawat mansanas, saging, o patatas sa tindahan ay produkto ng pagsasaka na ginawa ng tao, bago pa man may mga laboratorio. Sinasabi ni Tyson na ang mga modernong teknikang pang-genetic ay lamang ang susunod na hakbang sa isang pamamaraang dating kakaunti ang pag-aari ng pagsasaka — artificial selection. Bakit, tanong niya, dapat nating iwasan kapag umabot na ang teknolohiya mula sa mga bukid patungo sa mga test tube? Hinihikayat niya ang mga kritiko na subukan kumain ng isang wild apple — maalat, matigas, at puno ng buto — kung talagang gusto nila ang 'natural' na pagkain. Samantala, gumagamit ang mga siyentipiko ng modernong bioteknolohiya upang harapin ang mga malaking suliranin sa mundo. Sa Uganda, nagtatanim ang mga siyentipiko ng mga saging na may mataas na pro-vitamin A upang labanan ang pagkakaroon ng blindnes at kamatayan dahil sa kakulangan sa bitamina A, isang problema na nakakaapekto sa milyon-milyong mga bata tuwing taon sa Africa. Ang mga 'super banana' na ito ay hindi lang science fiction — lumalaman ang kanilang laman sa kulay orange habang tumataas ang antas ng nutrisyon, at nasa pagsisimula na ang mga klinikal na pagsubok. Ang mga pangunahing organisasyong siyentipiko, kabilang ang National Academy of Sciences at European Commission, ay sumasang-ayon: hindi raw maaaring maging mapanganib ang GMOs. Ang tunay na isyu ay hindi ang teknolohiya — kundi kung paano natin ito gagamitin nang matalino, pantay, at may transparensya.

article_content: As toxic smog blankets Delhi and nearby areas, India’s Union Health Ministry has issued a stark warning targeting children, calling air pollution an immediate threat to public health. Although rainfall on Friday brought temporary relief—lowering the city’s Air Quality Index (AQI) to 398 at 10:30 a.m.—many locations still registered 'Severe' levels, with one site hitting 407. The Central Pollution Control Board confirmed the fluctuating but dangerous air conditions. Schools are now urged to become frontline defenders against pollution. The Health Ministry advises educators and parents to actively teach students how to protect themselves: hold awareness drives, reward eco-friendly behavior, and keep windows shut when AQI rises. Indoor breaks are strongly recommended, and classrooms should be ventilated with exhaust fans—or opened only when air quality improves. To reduce exposure, schools are encouraged to switch from chalkboards to whiteboards, mop floors with water before students arrive, and promote cycling among older students. Electric school buses and vehicles are also highlighted as long-term solutions to cut emissions. Young children and those with pre-existing respiratory or heart conditions are especially at risk. Health officials stress that families should seek medical help immediately if symptoms like coughing, wheezing, or breathlessness appear. Beyond schools, state health departments are being asked to ramp up readiness: train medical staff, strengthen surveillance through sentinel hospitals under the NPCCHH program, and broadcast clear warnings in regional languages. Union Health Secretary Sudhansh Pant and DGHS Atul Goel both emphasized that pollution isn’t just causing short-term illness—it’s worsening chronic diseases across the board. Meanwhile, Delhi’s government is exploring extreme measures like artificial rain and has activated Stage IV of its emergency GRAP plan. Officials were seen inspecting pollution control efforts firsthand, signaling heightened urgency. While weather forecasts predict light rain and fog over the next two days, experts warn that without systemic reforms, these brief respites won’t solve the crisis.
translated_content: Habang ang toxic na smog ay nagsasakop sa Delhi at mga kalapit na lugar, ang Union Health Ministry ng India ay naglabas ng malalim na babala para sa mga bata, na tinuturing ang polusyon sa hangin bilang isang direktang banta sa pampublikong kalusugan. Bagaman ang ulan noong Biyernes ay nagdala ng pansamantalang pagpapalaya—bumaba ang Air Quality Index (AQI) ng lungsod sa 398 sa 10:30 a.m.—maraming lugar ay nanatili sa antas na 'Severe', na may isang lokasyon na umabot sa 407. Ang Central Pollution Control Board ay kumpirmado ang magkakaibang-unit ngunit mapanganib na kalagayan ng hangin. Ang mga paaralan ay ngayon ay hinihiling na maging unang linya ng pagtutol sa polusyon. Inirerekomenda ng Health Ministry na aktibong turuan ng mga guro at magulang ang mga estudyante kung paano protektahan ang kanilang sarili: mag-organisa ng mga kampanya sa kamalayan, bigyan ng parangal ang mga gawain na kaugnay sa kalikasan, at panatilihin ang mga bintana sa sarado kapag tumataas ang AQI. Ang mga pahinga sa loob ng silid ay malakas na inirerekomenda, at ang mga silid-aralan ay dapat bigyan ng sapat na pagpapalipad ng hangin gamit ang exhaust fans—o buksan lamang kapag mas maayos ang kalidad ng hangin. Upang mabawasan ang eksposur, inirerekomenda ng mga paaralan na palitan ang mga chalkboard sa whiteboards, mag-wet mopping sa mga sahig bago dumating ang mga mag-aaral, at suportahan ang paggamit ng bisikleta ng mga mas matatandang estudyante. Ang mga elektrikong sasakyan para sa paaralan ay itinuturing din bilang mahabang panahong solusyon upang bawasan ang emisyon. Ang mga mas batang bata at ang mga may pre-existing respiratory o heart conditions ay partikular na nasa panganib. Ibinigay ng mga opisyales ng kalusugan na dapat humingi ng medikal na tulong agad kung may sintomas tulad ng pagkabuhok, paghinga ng mahirap, o pagkakaroon ng hininga. Sa labas ng paaralan, hinihiling sa mga departamento ng kalusugan ng estado na palakasin ang paghahanda: magtrabaho sa pagtuturo sa mga manggagawa sa kalusugan, mapalakas ang pagmamasid sa pamamagitan ng mga sentinel hospital sa ilalim ng programa ng NPCCHH, at ipaabot ang malinaw na babala sa mga lokal na wika. Ang Union Health Secretary na si Sudhansh Pant at ang DGHS na si Atul Goel ay parehong nagteklaro na ang polusyon ay hindi lang nagdudulot ng pansamantaling sakit—ito ay nagpapalala sa mga kronikong sakit sa buong sistema. Samantala, ang gobyerno ng Delhi ay nagsasaliksik sa ekstremong hakbang tulad ng artificial rain at nakapag-activate na ng Stage IV ng kanilang emergency GRAP plan. Nakita ang mga opisyales na nagmamasid sa mga hakbang upang kontrolin ang polusyon, na nagpapakita ng mataas na urgensiya. Samantala, ang mga palatantiya ng panahon ay naghahayag ng kaunting ulan at mistula sa susunod na dalawang araw, ngunit ang mga eksperto ay babala na nang walang sistemikong reporma, ang mga pansamantalang pagpapalaya ay hindi lutasin ang krisis.

article_content: In a rare and tightly guarded move, Nigerian President Goodluck Jonathan traveled to Maiduguri — the heart of Boko Haram’s power — to meet survivors of one of the deadliest attacks in the group’s history. Over 2,500 people are believed to have been killed in the January assault on the towns of Baga and Doron Baga, where more than 3,700 buildings — including homes, schools, and markets — were reduced to ashes. Satellite images obtained by Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch revealed shocking destruction: nearly 60% of Doron Baga and over 10% of Baga were obliterated, likely by fire. Survivors described scenes of horror: militants shooting indiscriminately, killing children and even a woman in labor. Thousands now live in makeshift camps, clinging to hope after losing everything. In a heartfelt address to 5,000 displaced people, President Jonathan vowed to reclaim every territory held by Boko Haram. 'You will return to your homes,' he promised. This was his first visit to the region since 2013, coming after a prior trip was abruptly canceled. His administration has faced mounting criticism for failing to contain the insurgency, despite years of military efforts. Meanwhile, international leaders have not stayed silent. U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry labeled Boko Haram’s actions a 'crime against humanity,' while UN envoy Gordon Brown denounced the use of young girls as suicide bombers as 'barbaric.' A recent blast in Maiduguri killed at least 19 people, including many at a busy market, highlighting the group’s continued cruelty. In a sign of regional solidarity, Chad plans to send troops to support Cameroon in the fight. And still, 219 of the 276 girls abducted from Chibok in 2014 remain missing — a haunting reminder of the long shadow cast by this terror.

Sa higit sa 2,500 ang nanatili na namatay sa pag-atake sa Enero sa mga bayan ng Baga at Doron Baga, kung saan higit sa 3,700 na gusali — kabilang ang mga bahay, paaralan, at palengke — ay naging alimuot. Ang mga larawan mula sa kalawakan na natanggap ng Amnesty International at Human Rights Watch ay nagpakita ng nakakalulungkot na pagkasira: halos 60% ng Doron Baga at higit sa 10% ng Baga ay nalikas, malamang dahil sa apoy. Ang mga nakakita ay naglarawan ng mga eksena ng kahinaan: ang mga mangmang ay nagbubunot nang walang pagpapaliwanag, patay ang mga bata at kahit ang isang babae sa paglalang. Libu-libo ng tao ay naninirahan sa mga pansamantalang kamp, naghihintay ng pag-asa matapos mawalan ng lahat. Sa isang malalim na talakayan sa 5,000 na nangibang-bayan, pangako ni Pangulong Jonathan na muling kunin ang bawat teritoryo na nasa kontrol ng Boko Haram. 'Mabalik kayo sa inyong mga bahay,' sinabi niya. Ito ang kanyang unang pagbisita sa rehiyon mula noong 2013, na sumunod sa isang dating pagbisita na ikinansela sa huling sandali. Ang kanyang administrasyon ay nakakaranas ng malaking pagmamaliw para sa kahinaan nito sa pagpigil sa rebelyon, bagaman mayroon nang taon-taon na militar na pagsisikap. Samantala, hindi tumigil ang mga internasyonal na lider. Ang Sekretarya ng Estado ng Estados Unidos na si John Kerry ay tinawag ang mga aksyon ng Boko Haram bilang 'krimen laban sa sangkatauhan,' habang ang tagapagtaguyod ng UN para sa edukasyon na si Gordon Brown ay kinondena ang paggamit ng mga batang babae bilang mga bombang pantao bilang 'barbaro.' Isang bagong pag-atake sa Maiduguri ay namatay sa higit sa 19 na tao, kabilang ang marami sa isang puno ng palengke, na nagpapakita ng patuloy na kabiguan ng grupo. Bilang tanda ng regional na pagkakaisa, planuhin ng Chad na ipadala ang mga sundalo upang tulungan ang Cameroon sa pakikidigma. At pa rin, 219 sa 276 na batang babae na sinupil sa Chibok noong 2014 ay nananatiling nawawala — isang malungkot na paalala ng mahabang anino na itinatapon ng teror na ito.

article_content: As a young boy, Mark Pearson watched his mother scour newspapers for coupons to afford milk and bread for their family. Now one of Britain’s wealthiest entrepreneurs, worth an estimated £60 million, he credits that humble beginning as the driving force behind his success. Growing up in Huyton, Liverpool, Pearson endured a difficult childhood. His mother, Julie, worked multiple low-paying jobs—often including night shifts at a petrol station—to support him and his younger sister, Alison. Financial strain forced them to stay frequently with his grandmother, who saved every coupon and watched every penny. On Christmas Day in 1992, after a violent incident with her partner, Julie took her children to a women’s refuge. At just nine years old, Pearson felt the weight of becoming the man of the house. 'I felt I was now the only man in the family,' he recalls. That sense of responsibility ignited a lifelong determination to provide. After working as a chef under Gordon Ramsay and running a floristry business, Pearson launched My Voucher Codes in November 2006 from a one-bedroom flat in Croydon, investing just £300. He spent hours collecting discount codes from magazines and websites, posting them online and earning commissions through affiliate marketing. Within a year, the site generated £300,000 in revenue. Four years later, earnings hit £10 million. By 2011, he was named Ernst & Young’s Emerging Entrepreneur of the Year. In June, Monitise plc acquired Markco Media, the parent company of My Voucher Codes, for £55 million. With his newfound wealth, Pearson bought his mother a home in Liverpool—and later, a property in Barbados. Today, she splits her time between the two homes. He also purchased a home for himself, his partner Arron Harpin, and their two surrogate twin sons. 'One of the things I’m most proud of,' Pearson says, 'is giving something back to my mum. The look on her face when I gave her the house? Indescribable. That’s when I knew I’d made it.' Though he now owns luxury cars and divides his time between Britain and the Caribbean, Pearson remains grounded. 'Unlike roses,' he jokes, 'I’m selling something that doesn’t cost me anything to buy.'

Ngayon, bilang isa sa mga pinakamayaman na negosyante sa Britanya, na may halagang humigit-kumulang na £60 milyon, iniuugnay niya ang kanyang simpleng paglaki bilang dahilan ng kanyang tagumpay. Nagdaraan si Pearson sa isang mahirap na kabataan sa Huyton, Liverpool. Ang kanyang ina, Julie, ay nagtrabaho sa maraming mababaw na trabaho—kadalasang gabi sa isang gas station—upang suportahan siya at ang kanyang mas bata kapatid na babae, Alison. Dahil sa kakulangan sa pera, madalas silang tumira sa bahay ng kanyang lola, na nag-iipon ng bawat coupon at pinagmamasdan ang bawat piso. Noong Pasko noong 1992, matapos ang isang pang-aabuso mula sa kasintahan ng kanyang ina, dinala ni Julie ang kanyang mga anak sa isang refuge para sa mga babae. Sa edad na siyam lang, nadama ni Pearson ang bigat na maging lalaking tao sa pamilya. 'Naramdaman ko na ako ang tanging lalaki sa pamilya,' sabi niya. Ang pagkakaroon ng ganitong responsibilidad ay nag-udyok sa kanya ng isang habambuhay na determinasyon na magbigay. Matapos magtrabaho bilang isang chef kay Gordon Ramsay at magtatag ng isang negosyo ng bulaklak, itinatag ni Pearson ang My Voucher Codes noong Nobyembre 2006 mula sa isang isang-silid na apartment sa Croydon, na nag-invest ng £300 lamang. Naghihintay siya nang maraming oras upang kumuha ng mga code ng diskwento mula sa mga magazine at website, at isinasampa ito online upang makakuha ng komisyon sa pamamagitan ng affiliate marketing. Sa loob ng isang taon, ang site ay nagkamit ng £300,000 sa kita. Sa loob ng apat na taon, tumubo ang kita hanggang £10 milyon. Noong 2011, napili siyang Emerging Entrepreneur of the Year ng Ernst & Young. Noong Hunyo, kinuha ni Monitise plc ang Markco Media, ang parent company ng My Voucher Codes, para sa £55 milyon. Gamit ang kanyang bagong-kamit na yaman, bumili si Pearson ng bahay para sa kanyang ina sa Liverpool—at huli, isang properti sa Barbados. Ngayon, hihiwalay niya ang kanyang panahon sa dalawang lugar. Bumili rin siya ng bahay para sa kanya, ang kanyang kasintahan na si Arron Harpin, at ang kanilang dalawang anak na twins na ipinanganak sa pamamagitan ng surrogate. 'Ang isa sa mga bagay na pinakamaligaya kong natamo,' sabi ni Pearson, 'ay ibinigay ang kanyang balik sa aking ina. Ang ekspresyon sa kanyang mukha nang ibigay ko sa kanya ang bahay? Hindi maipapaliwanag. Nung iyon, alam kong naging tagumpay na ako.' Bagaman ngayon ay mayroon siyang mga luxury car at hihiwalay ang kanyang oras sa pagitan ng Britanya at ang Caribbean, nananatiling mapagmoderadong si Pearson. article_content: Suspended Miami Dolphins guard Richie Incognito claims he received threatening text messages from former teammate Jonathan Martin—and that their communication was often vulgar, but mutually understood as good-natured banter. In an interview with Fox’s NFL Sunday, Incognito stated that he and other offensive linemen frequently used aggressive language, insisting it was part of their team culture. He shared a text from Martin that read: 'I will murder your whole effing family.' According to Fox Sports reporter Jay Glazer, the two exchanged 1,142 texts over the past year, many too vulgar for broadcast. Incognito expressed embarrassment that the messages were made public but maintained they were private jokes between friends. 'I knew it was coming from a friend, from a teammate—that puts context on the words,' he said. He added that Martin also used similar language, citing it as evidence of mutual rapport. Days after Martin left the team, he texted Incognito: 'Wassup man? The world’s gotten crazy LOL I’m good tho. Congrats on the win.' Martin later denied sending the explicit messages publicly and said he didn’t know how they surfaced. In another message, Martin wrote: 'Yeah, I’m good man. It’s insane bro, but just know that I don’t blame you guys at all—it’s just the culture around football and the locker room got to me a little.' Incognito insisted he 'never meant to hurt anyone' and that the messages were intended as humor among friends. 'It sounds like I’m a racist pig or a meathead—but I’m not those things. I’m a good person,' he said. He described Martin as his best friend on the team and challenged others to ask any Dolphin: 'Who had John’s back the absolute most? It was me.' Incognito claimed Martin never indicated the language bothered him, and that the media’s portrayal of him as a bully is inaccurate. He admitted using the n-word, acknowledging it was wrong—even if common in locker rooms—and said, 'In no way, shape, or form is it right for me to use that word.' Incognito thanked teammates who defended him during media scrutiny, saying, 'All this stuff coming out speaks to the culture of our locker room—the culture of our closeness, our brotherhood.' He said he would apologize to Martin and his family if given the chance: 'I’d give him a big hug and say, 'Dude, what’s going on?' If he said I took it too far, I’d apologize—fully.' The interview, conducted in Los Angeles by Glazer, followed new allegations: in 2012, a woman accused Incognito of sexually assaulting her during the Fins Weekend Golf Tournament at Turnberry Resort and Club. According to a police report obtained by WPLG, Incognito allegedly used a golf club to rub the woman’s private areas, knocked off her glasses, danced against her buttocks, and poured bottled water on her face—all while intoxicated. The woman reported that bystanders witnessed the behavior but did not intervene. She said she filed the report because Incognito never apologized and acted as if it was 'fun and games.' Team security was informed but reportedly took no action. This is the third major scandal involving Incognito, following the release of racially charged voicemails and a viral video of him drunkenly shouting the n-word in a bar. Incognito remains suspended pending an NFL investigation into allegations of racism and abuse. Martin has left the team for counseling and accused unnamed teammates of threatening to rape his sister. While some teammates support Incognito, claiming language was misinterpreted, others are bewildered by Martin’s decision to go public. A source told ESPN Incognito felt 'blindsided and betrayed.' The Dolphins have not publicly responded to the latest allegations.

Ito ay ang ikatlong malaking skandalo na nauugnay kay Incognito, matapos ang paglabas ng mga rasyal na mensahe at isang viral na video kung saan siya ay nakapagmumura ng n-word habang nasa ilalim ng impluwensiya ng alak sa isang bar. Nasa ilalim pa rin ng suspensiyon si Incognito habang sinusuri ng NFL ang alegasyon ng rasismo at pang-aabuso. Umalis na si Martin sa koponan para sa konselyo at inakusahan ang ilang kasamahan na bantaan na pagnanakaw sa kanyang kapatid na babae. Habang may ilang kasamahan na sumusuporta kay Incognito, sinasabing mali ang pag-unawa sa wika, may iba pa na nahihirapan na maintindihan ang desisyon ni Martin na maglabas. article_content: At just 11 years old, Quvenzhané Wallis — the youngest-ever Best Actress Oscar nominee — didn’t hold back during a recent interview with New York Times Style. When asked to reflect on balancing Hollywood fame with schoolwork, she responded with a yawn and admitted, 'It gets a little boring.' She wasn’t rude, just real. After politely agreeing to three more questions — 'Make them big so I can answer them big' — she declared, 'We’re done now,' clearly eager to get back to her video games. Even when the conversation turned to her acclaimed co-stars Jamie Foxx and Cameron Diaz, who’ve praised her talent enthusiastically, her enthusiasm stayed low. Describing them simply as 'really nice,' she rolled her eyes at deeper questions about inspiration. Her honesty wasn’t defiance; it was childhood. She explained, 'I don’t have any jokes to tell because the questions are so serious.' Instead of playing along with the usual celebrity script, she challenged reporter Nicholas Haramis to a game of Hoop Fever, betting him $1 if he lost. And she didn’t act like a star off-camera either: at school, her friends see her as just Quvenzhané — not a movie icon. 'They take me as a friend because I'm their friend,' she said. While her interview style may seem unpolished, her career is anything but. She’s the face of Armani Junior, stars in the upcoming Annie remake, and has two more films lined up for next year. But despite the red carpets and billboards, her world hasn’t changed much. As she put it, strangers might stare — but her friends? They just want to play.

article_content: Everton captain Phil Jagielka has bounced back from his World Cup struggles and is now riding a remarkable run of clean sheets heading into Sunday’s clash against Burnley. The 32-year-old center-back has gone four matches without conceding a goal — for both club and country — following a hard-fought Europa League draw in Lille on Thursday. Another shutout at Turf Moor would mark his fifth consecutive clean sheet, the first such streak since the end of the 2012/13 season. This resurgence comes after Jagielka faced heavy criticism for his role in England’s group-stage exits against Italy and Uruguay earlier in the summer. But recent performances have silenced many doubters. Beyond his defensive solidity, Jagielka has added goals to his game this season, finding the net against San Marino, Liverpool, and Aston Villa. 'Keeping clean sheets is what my game is all about,' he said. 'If I can chip in with an occasional goal, all the better — but as a defender, my job is to stop the ball from going in.' He acknowledges that early-season struggles were amplified by pundits, but insists his form was never as bad as portrayed. 'Then I score a couple of goals and suddenly I’m a better player? That’s just how football works.' Since Everton’s 2-1 defeat at Manchester United on October 5, Jagielka has played in four matches — two for England and two for Everton — and not once has a goalkeeper had to retrieve the ball from the net. Manager Roberto Martinez has praised Jagielka’s consistency, especially given the constant changes in his defensive partners: John Stones, Antolin Alcaraz, Sylvain Distin, Gary Cahill, and even Tony Hibbert, who stepped in against Lille. 'It’s been tough with all the injuries and fixture congestion,' Jagielka admitted. 'But it felt great to keep a clean sheet with Sylvain again — we haven’t played together in ages.' One highlight: Jagielka helped neutralize Lille’s £10 million striker Divock Origi, on loan from Liverpool. 'He looked dangerous, but we handled him,' he said. Everton’s 3-0 win over Aston Villa last weekend was only their second Premier League victory of the season — and has lifted them clear of the relegation zone. With Burnley still searching for their first win, Jagielka and his teammates are determined to extend their momentum — and their clean sheet streak — on Sunday.

Ang 32-taong-gulang na center-back ay hindi nagbigay ng anumang goal sa apat na match — parehong para sa kanyang klub at bansa — matapos ang isang mahigpit na pagkakapareho sa Europa League sa Lille noong Huwebes. Isang bagong clean sheet sa Turf Moor ay gagawin itong limang patuloy na clean sheet, ang unang ganitong serye mula pa noong wakas ng 2012/13 season. Ang pagbabalik na ito ay sumunod sa malakas na kritika na tinanggap ni Jagielka dahil sa kanyang papel sa pagkatalo ng England laban sa Italy at Uruguay sa panahon ng summer. Bukod sa kanyang katatagan sa depensa, nakapuntos din si Jagielka sa season na ito laban sa San Marino, Liverpool, at Aston Villa. 'Ang pagpapanatili ng clean sheets ang pangunahing layunin ko,' sabi niya. 'Kung makakapuntos ako ng ilang beses, mas magandang mas mainam — pero bilang defender, ang tungkulin ko ay pigilan ang bola na pumasok.' 'Pagkatapos kong makapuntos ng dalawang beses, biglang ako'y mas mabuting manlalaro? Ganito lang ang football.' Mula pa noong pagkatalo ng Everton sa 2-1 laban sa Manchester United noong Oktubre 5, si Jagielka ay nakapaglaro sa apat na match — dalawa para sa England at dalawa para sa kanyang klub — at hindi isang beses natanggap ng manlalaro ang bola sa net. Ang tagapamahala ni Roberto Martinez ay nagpupuri sa konsistensya ni Jagielka, lalo na dahil sa paulit-ulit na pagbabago ng kanyang mga kasamahan sa backline: John Stones, Antolin Alcaraz, Sylvain Distin, Gary Cahill, at kahit si Tony Hibbert, na pumasok laban sa Lille. 'Nakikita kong banta siya, ngunit nakaharap natin siya,' sabi niya. Ang 3-0 na panalo ng Everton laban sa Aston Villa noong nakaraang linggo ay ang kanilang ikalawang panalo sa Premier League sa season na ito — at nagpalaya sa kanila sa mababang bahagi ng tabela. Habang hinahanap pa rin ng Burnley ang kanilang unang panalo, gustong-layunin ni Jagielka at ang kanyang mga kasamahan na palawakin ang kanilang momentum — at ang kanilang serye ng clean sheets — sa Linggo.

article_content: At 72, Norman Croucher has summited more than 100 mountains across the globe — from the Himalayas to the Alps — despite losing both legs in a train accident at age 19. Doctors told him climbing was over, but he refused to let that be the end of his story. Instead, he turned rehabilitation into a lifelong passion, scaling cliffs near his home in Devon as soon as he got his first prosthetics. Today, he doesn’t see his amputation as a barrier — in fact, he believes it helps. With less body mass and a shorter circulatory system, he claims to retain heat better and oxygenate more efficiently than able-bodied climbers, sometimes reaching peaks ahead of others. He’s even found practical perks on long flights: removing his prosthetics lets him stretch out across two seats for a restful nap. His feats include being the first amputee to walk the full 900-mile route from John O’Groats to Land’s End in 1969, and pioneering accessible adventures like sailing and zip-lining for people with disabilities. Recently diagnosed with bowel cancer, Croucher isn’t slowing down. In June, he’ll join two friends to tackle several 11,500-foot peaks near Chamonix, raising money for Exeter Hospiscare. 'Climbing is an addiction,' he says. 'Life’s like a muscle — if you don’t stretch it, it withers.' For him, every peak is a reminder that limits are often just stories we tell ourselves.

Sinabi ng mga doktor na tapos na ang klimbing para sa kanya, ngunit tinanggihan niya na tanggapin iyon bilang wakas ng kanyang kuwento. Sa halip, isinulong niya ang rehabilitasyon bilang isang habambuhay na pagkukulang, at sinikat ang mga klawe sa malapit sa kanyang tahanan sa Devon agad pagkatapos makakuha ng kanyang unang prostetiko. Ngayon, hindi niya itinuturing ang pagkawala ng kanyang mga paa bilang hadlang — sa katotohanan, naniniwala siya na nakakatulong ito. Dahil mas kaunti ang kanyang bigat at mas maikli ang kanyang sirkulasyon, sinasabi niya na mas mabuting nagpapanatili siya ng init at mas epektibo ang kanyang pag-oxygenate kaysa sa mga klimbeng walang kapansanan, at minsan ay nakarating muna sa tuktok kaysa sa iba. Kahit na nakakahanap siya ng praktikal na benepisyo sa mahahabang paglalakbay sa eroplano: ang pag-alis ng kanyang mga prostetiko ay nagpapahintulot sa kanya na magpalawak sa dalawang upuan para sa isang mas mainam na pagtulog. Ang kanyang mga tagumpay ay kasama ang pagiging unang amputado na maglakad sa buong 900-milya na rutas mula sa John O'Groats hanggang sa Land's End noong 1969, at pagpapakilala ng mga accessible na gawaing pang-adventura tulad ng paglalayag at pag-zipline para sa mga may kapansanan. Kamakailan lamang ay dinagdagan ng kanser sa bituka, hindi nagpapabagal si Croucher. Para sa kanya, bawat tuktok ay paalala na ang mga hadlang ay karaniwang mga kuwento lamang na itinataglay natin sa atin.

article_content: Samalut, Egypt (CNN) — A police officer fatally shot a Christian man and wounded five others on a train in Egypt on Tuesday, officials said. The incident occurred around 5 p.m. when a man boarded a train stopped at the Samalut station, approximately 200 kilometers south of Cairo. Maryanne Nabil Thaki, 29, one of the victims, said she was seated with her sister, Maggie Nabil Thaki, 25; their 52-year-old mother, Sabah Sinot Suleiman; and Maggie’s fiancé, 26-year-old Ehab Ashraf Kamal. They were traveling to Cairo to buy an engagement ring, Maggie Thaki said. Nearby sat an elderly Christian couple, according to Maryanne Nabil Thaki. The gunman walked along the train, then returned to two nearby groups of Coptic Christians and shouted in Arabic, 'There is no God but God,' before opening fire, she recounted while being treated for gunshot wounds to the leg and chest at Good Shepherd Hospital in Samalut. The suspect fled but was later apprehended, according to a spokesperson for the Interior Ministry. The suspect, identified as Amer Ashoor Abdel-Zaher Hassan, a deputy police officer, had boarded the train in Asyut and was traveling to Bani Mazar in Menya Province, where he worked. The elderly man, Fathi Saeed Ebaid, 71, of Cairo, was killed, according to a local security source cited by the state-run Egyptian news agency MENA. His wife, Emily Hannah Tedly, 61, was in critical condition, as was the mother of the two younger women, Dr. Petra Kamal confirmed. All five survivors were scheduled to be flown to Cairo for further treatment, a hospital employee said. Outside the hospital, about a dozen Coptic demonstrators gathered in support of the victims but were dispersed by police, who fired a tear gas canister that shattered a fifth-floor hospital window, according to hospital employee Mina Farouk. The attack came ten days after a bombing killed 23 Coptic Christians outside the Church of the Two Saints in Alexandria — an incident that heightened fears among Egypt’s Christian community and prompted increased security measures. Relations between Egypt’s Christian minority and Muslim majority have remained tense since the New Year’s Day bombing. On Christmas Day — celebrated by Copts following the Julian calendar — police conducted a large-scale security operation outside the same church. Some Egyptian Muslims attended the services in solidarity, yet protests have erupted nearly nightly in Christian neighborhoods since the bombing. Egyptian authorities have released a facial reconstruction of the suspected suicide bomber from the Alexandria attack, created using forensic technology. Approximately 9% of Egypt’s 80 million residents are Coptic Christians. Their faith traces its origins to the Apostle Mark, who introduced Christianity to Egypt, according to St. Mark’s Cathedral in Alexandria, the spiritual center of Coptic Christianity. The Coptic Orthodox Church split from other Christian denominations in the fifth century over theological disputes regarding the nature of Christ’s divinity. CNN’s Ben Wedeman, Housam Ahmed, Amir Ahmed, and journalist Ian Lee contributed to this report.

Nangyari ang insidente sa halos 5 ng hapon nang pumasok ang isang lalake sa isang tren na nakapila sa istasyon ng Samalut, humigit-kumulang 200 kilometro timog ng Cairo. Si Maryanne Nabil Thaki, 29, isa sa mga biktima, ay nagsabi na siya ay nakaupo kasama ang kanyang kapatid na babae, si Maggie Nabil Thaki, 25; ang kanilang 52-taong-gulang na ina, si Sabah Sinot Suleiman; at ang panginoon ni Maggie, si Ehab Ashraf Kamal, 26. Naglalakbay sila papuntang Cairo para bumili ng isang pambihirang singsing, ayon kay Maggie Thaki. Malapit sa kanila ay nakaupo ang isang matandang mag-asawang Kristiyano, ayon kay Maryanne Nabil Thaki. Ang tagapagbanta ay lumakad sa buong haba ng tren, pagkatapos ay bumalik sa dalawang grupo ng mga Coptic na Kristiyano na nakaupo malapit sa bawat isa at sinigaw sa wikang Arabic, 'Walang Diyos kundi ang Diyos,' bago tumira, ayon sa kanya habang tinatanggap ang paggamot sa mga sugat ng baril sa binti at dibdib sa Good Shepherd Hospital sa Samalut. Ang suspect ay tumakas ngunit isinakdal muli, ayon sa isang tagapagsalita ng Kagawaran ng Interyor. Ang suspect, na kilala bilang Amer Ashoor Abdel-Zaher Hassan, isang tanggapan ng pulis, ay pumasok sa tren sa Asyut at naglalakbay patungo sa Bani Mazar sa probinsya ng Menya, kung saan siya nagtatrabaho. Ang matandang lalake, si Fathi Saeed Ebaid, 71, mula sa Cairo, ay namatay, ayon sa isang lokal na pinagkukunan ng seguridad na binanggit ng pampublikong ahensya ng Ehipto na MENA. Nangyari ang pag-atake sampu't anim na araw pagkatapos ng isang pagpapahid na namatay sa 23 Coptic na Kristiyano labas ng Simbahan ng Dalawang Santo sa Alexandria, Ehipto — isang insidente na nagpalakas ng takot sa komunidad ng mga Kristiyano at nagdulot ng mas malaking seguridad. Ang ugnayan sa pagitan ng maliliit na komunidad ng Kristiyano at karamihan ng Muslim sa Ehipto ay nananatiling hindi maayos mula pa noong pag-atake sa Bagong Taon. Noong Pasko — na ipinagdiriwang ng mga Coptic na sumusunod sa Julian calendar — ang pulis ay nagtayo ng malaking operasyon ng seguridad labas sa parehong simbahan. Ang ilang Muslim na Ehiptiyano ay dumalo sa serbisyo ng Pasko bilang pagpapakita ng suporta, ngunit ang mga protesta ay lumitaw halos tuwing gabi sa mga lugar ng mga Kristiyano mula pa noong pag-atake. Ang mga awtoridad sa Ehipto ay naglabas ng isang larawan ng isang lalake na kanilang inaasahang siyang suicide bomber sa pag-atake sa simbahan, na ginawa gamit ang teknolohiya ng forensic. Humigit-kumulang 9% ng 80 milyong tao sa Ehipto ay mga Coptic na Kristiyano. Ang kanilang paniniwala ay nagsimula sa apostol na si Marcos, na ipinakilala ang Kristiyanismo sa Ehipto, ayon sa Katedral ni San Marcos sa Alexandria, ang espirituwal na sentro ng Coptic Christianity. Ang simbahan ng Coptic ay naging hiwalay sa iba pang mga Kristiyanong denominasyon noong ika-limang siglo dahil sa mga diskusyon tungkol sa kalikasan ng pagkadiyos ni Cristo.
