article_content: After seven long years in shelters, a lurcher named Jed is still waiting for his forever home — despite being described as loving, calm indoors, and great with other dogs. Taken in by the Dogs Trust at just four months old, Jed has been returned twice: once because his first family thought he was too lively, and again when their personal situation changed. Since then, nearly 17,000 potential adopters have passed him by. Carers say Jed isn’t the problem — misconceptions are. Many assume lurchers need hours of intense exercise, but in reality, Jed thrives with moderate walks and plenty of cuddles. He spends his days lounging on a cozy duvet in the office, bonding with staff, playing with toys, and chasing friends across the field — then crashing for a nap. The Dogs Trust stresses that Jed needs someone with experience handling energetic dogs, a consistent routine, and the flexibility to be home part-time so he doesn’t feel lonely. While most dogs find homes within a month, Jed has outlasted the average by years. Even Battersea Dogs Home, which typically sees dogs stay no longer than two years, calls his seven-year stay 'unheard of' and a matter of terrible luck. His story echoes that of Casey, a cat who waited 13 years for adoption, highlighting how deeply misunderstood some animals remain, even when they’re perfectly suited for quiet, loving homes.
translated_content: Pagkatapos ng pitong taon sa shelter, ang isang lurcher na si Jed ay patuloy pa ring naghihintay ng isang tanging bahay — bagaman tinatawag siyang mahal, mapayapa sa loob ng bahay, at mabuting kasama ng ibang aso. Kinuha siya ng Dogs Trust nang siya ay apat na buwan lang, at dalawang beses siyang binalik: una dahil sa paniniwala ng kanyang unang pamilya na sobrang aktibo siya, at pangalawa naman dahil sa pagbabago sa kanilang personal na sitwasyon. Mula noon, halos 17,000 posibleng tagapag-adop ay syang pinabayaan. Sinasabi ng mga tagapag-alaga na hindi si Jed ang problema — ang mga kamalian ang problema. Marami ang naniniwala na kailangan ng mga lurcher ng maraming oras ng intensibong ehersisyo, ngunit sa katotohanan, mas nakikinabang si Jed sa moderadong paglalakad at maraming pagmamahal. Pasok niya ang araw sa pamamagitan ng pagpapahinga sa isang kumportableng duvet sa opisina, pagkakaroon ng ugnayan sa mga manggagawa, paglalaro ng mga laruan, at pagtakbo kasama ang kanyang mga kaibigan sa field — at pagkatapos ay pagsisidli para sa isang kuwarto. Ipinapahiwatig ng Dogs Trust na kailangan ni Jed ng isang tao na may karanasan sa pag-aalaga ng aktibong mga aso, isang tiyak na routine, at kakayahang magkaroon ng bahagyang oras sa bahay upang hindi siya makaramdam ng kalungkutan. Samantalang karaniwang natutuklasan ng mga aso ang kanilang bahay sa loob ng isang buwan, lumampas na ni Jed sa average sa loob ng mga taon. Kahit ang Battersea Dogs Home, na karaniwang nakikita ang mga aso na nagtatagal ng hindi hihigit sa dalawang taon, tinatawag na 'hindi naririto bago' ang kanyang pitong-taong paghihintay at isang kaso ng malaking kasamaan. Ang kanyang kuwento ay tumutugma sa kuwento ni Casey, isang pusa na naghintay ng 13 taon para sa isang bahay, na nagpapakita kung gaano kadalas na mali ang pag-unawa sa ilang hayop, kahit na perpekto sila para sa tahimik, mapagmahal na tahanan.

article_content: Darren Sanders, the security director of the Baltimore Ravens, is set to appear in court on a charge of fourth-degree sexual assault. The alleged incident occurred on December 14 and is classified as non-violent under Maryland law, carrying a maximum penalty of a $1,000 fine, up to one year in jail, or both. Individuals with prior convictions may face up to three years in prison. Court records filed by the Baltimore City District Court list Sanders’ address as the Ravens’ headquarters in Owings Mills, Maryland. His hearing is scheduled for February 9, though specific details of the case remain undisclosed. Sanders’ attorney, Andrew Alperstein, has strongly denied the allegations, calling them 'totally fabricated' and arguing that false accusations undermine the credibility of real survivors. 'People like [Sanders] are susceptible to made-up allegations,' Alperstein said. 'He's had nothing but an exemplary career.' The Ravens organization confirmed it is aware of the charges and has initiated its own internal review. Sanders has been with the team for over a decade and was a visible figure during the 2014 investigation into former player Ray Rice, who was caught on video assaulting his then-fiancée, Janay Palmer, in an Atlantic City elevator. At the time, Sanders publicly denied claims that he had contacted police immediately after the incident. The NFL initially imposed a two-game suspension and $500,000 fine on Rice, prompting widespread public outrage. After the full video surfaced, the Ravens terminated Rice’s $40 million contract. The scandal drew national attention, including criticism from then-President Barack Obama.

Maaaring makahingga ng hanggang tatlong taon ang mga may nakaraang kaso. Ang mga tala sa korte na ipinasa ng Baltimore City District Court ay naglalaman ng address ni Sanders bilang opisina ng Ravens sa Owings Mills, Maryland. Ang pagkikita niya ay jadwal sa Pebrero 9, bagaman ang mga detalye ng kaso ay hindi pa nalalaman. Ang abogado ni Sanders, si Andrew Alperstein, ay kinabiglaan ang mga akusasyon, tinawag itong 'kumpletong ginawa-gawa' at sinabi na ang mga maling akusasyon ay nagpapakalat sa kredibilidad ng mga tunay na biktima. 'Ang mga tao tulad ni [Sanders] ay madaling maging biktima ng mga ginawa-gawang akusasyon,' sabi ni Alperstein. 'Wala siyang naging karera kundi isang halimbawang karera.' Nagtapat ang organisasyon ng Ravens na kilala nila ang mga akusasyon at nagsisimula na ng kanilang sariling pananaliksik. Si Sanders ay kasama na sa koponan sa higit sa sampung taon at isang nakikita na figura sa pagsisiyasat ng 2014 laban sa dating laroy na si Ray Rice, na natangkap sa video habang pinipilit ang kanyang asawa, si Janay Palmer, sa loob ng isang elevator sa Atlantic City. Sa panahong iyon, kinabiglaan ni Sanders ang mga ulat na siya ay nakikipag-ugnayan sa pulis agad pagkatapos ng insidente. Ang NFL ay unang ipinagkaloob ang dalawang laro na suspensyon at $500,000 na multa kay Rice, na nagdulot ng malawakang pagtutol. Pagkatapos lumabas ang buong video, tinanggal ng Ravens ang kontrata ni Rice na halos $40 milyon. Ang skandalo ay nakakuha ng pansin sa bansa, kabilang ang pagkakalat ng kritika mula kay dating Pangulo Barack Obama.

article_content: By Martha De Lacey. PUBLISHED: 08:06 EST, 4 October 2013. | UPDATED: 09:43 EST, 4 October 2013. A bride who waited 12 years to marry her fiancé because she feared appearing overweight in wedding photos has lost nine stone — and wore a dress for the first time in her life. Jane Bailey, 38, from Staffordshire, previously consumed a diet high in chocolate and pastries, weighed 20 stone 9 pounds, and was nicknamed 'The Big One' and 'Big Jane' by colleagues. With a waistline of 46 inches, she had never felt confident enough to wear a dress. Jane and her fiancé, Andy, 48, became engaged 12 years earlier but postponed wedding plans until January 2011, when Jane found a wedding dress she loved and resolved to lose weight to fit into it. She immediately joined her local Slimming World group. Over the next two years, Jane lost nine stone through healthy eating, dropping from a size 26 to a size 12. On June 14, 2013, she walked down the aisle in a stunning empire-line gown — the first dress she had ever worn. Jane, who now weighs a healthy 11 stone 9 pounds, said: 'I had been engaged to Andy for 12 years, but I kept putting off setting a date because I didn’t want to look big on my wedding day. I used to eat things like chocolate and custard tarts in secret. People called me 'The Big One' or 'Big Jane.' Although I was mostly teased as a teen, I knew I had to change — especially for my wedding.' She joined Slimming World in January 2011, lost about six stone in the first year, and married Andy three months after reaching her target weight. The wedding marked a turning point. 'It was the first dress I ever wore — and it was my dream dress,' Jane said. 'I never wore dresses before because I was tomboyish when I was larger — I lived in jeans and T-shirts.' Her new role as an IT trainer at the University Hospital of North Staffordshire also motivated her. 'I was standing in front of doctors and nurses all day and felt judged. I needed to feel comfortable in my own skin.' Jane now enjoys shopping for clothes and grooming, saying: 'I have the confidence and the figure to wear more dresses — and it feels amazing.' Andy, who owns a hardware store, said: 'She looked beautiful walking down the aisle — she looked like a completely different woman. She’s worked so hard, and I’m so proud of her.' Jane will compete in the national 'Slimmer of the Year' finals in Birmingham.

article_content: Fifty years after Martin Luther King Jr.’s iconic 'I Have a Dream' speech, it’s easy to forget that the civil rights icon was once targeted by the FBI as if he were Public Enemy No. 1 — a label coined by media and amplified by Hoover’s office, though never officially designated. Under J. Edgar Hoover’s leadership, King was subjected to invasive surveillance: phones tapped, hotel rooms bugged, and associates paid to report his movements. These tactics, though crude by today’s standards, operated without judicial oversight at the time. What began as an investigation into alleged communist ties soon turned into a personal crusade; by October 10, 1963, Attorney General Robert F. Kennedy authorized intensified monitoring, privately calling King 'the most dangerous Negro in America.' Fast forward to today, and the FBI under former Director Robert Mueller claims to have evolved. Mueller emphasized that modern surveillance operates within strict legal boundaries, prioritizing national security threats like terrorism over political dissent. The bureau now dedicates significant resources to prosecuting police misconduct, hate crimes, and human trafficking — areas where accountability matters deeply. In 2012 alone, 42% of its civil rights investigations focused on 'color of law' abuses — excessive force, false arrests, and evidence fabrication by officials. Yet, disturbing parallels linger. Recent disclosures about the NSA reveal that government agents have used mass surveillance tools to spy on romantic partners, intercept private phone calls, and even delete intimate conversations out of discomfort — not out of protocol. One former NSA analyst, Adrienne Kinne, admitted to erasing recordings of Americans talking quietly to loved ones late at night, calling it 'incredibly personal' and unnecessary to record. King himself, as documented by Pulitzer Prize-winning biographer David Garrow, was deeply humble — driven by service, not fame. But the FBI seized on his private missteps, twisting them into ammunition. Today, we have better laws, oversight bodies, and ethical guidelines — but human temptation doesn’t disappear with technology. When powerful tools exist, and accountability is hidden behind secrecy, history has a way of repeating itself. The question isn’t just whether we’ve changed — it’s whether we’re brave enough to keep watching those who watch us.
translated_content: Limang pung taon pagkatapos ng sikat na talumpati ni Martin Luther King Jr. na 'I Have a Dream', madaling kalimutan na ang lider sa sibil na karapatan ay isang pangunahing layunin ng FBI — isang label na ginawa ng media at pinalakas ng opisina ni Hoover, bagaman hindi opisyal na ipinagkaloob. Sa ilalim ng pamumuno ni J. Edgar Hoover, sinubukan ni King ang masusing pagmamasid: tinapayan ang telepono, binugso ang mga kuwarto ng hotel, at binayaran ang mga kasamahan para magbigay ng impormasyon tungkol sa kanyang galaw. Ang mga taktika na ito, bagaman primitibo ayon sa mga istandard ngayon, ay gumana nang walang pagsusuri ng hukuman. Ang pag-aaral na nagsimula bilang pagsisiyasat sa posibleng ugnayan sa komunismo ay naging isang personal na pakikidigma; noong Oktubre 10, 1963, pinayagan ni Attorney General Robert F. Kennedy ang mas malakas na pagmamasid, at pribadong tinawag si King bilang 'pinakamapanganib na Negrito sa Amerika.' Lumipat tayo sa ngayon, at sinasabi ng FBI sa ilalim ng dating direktor na si Robert Mueller na nabago na nila ito. Binigyang-diin ni Mueller na ang modernong pagmamasid ay gumagana sa loob ng mahigpit na batas, at nagpapababa sa mga banta sa pambansang kaligtasan tulad ng terorismo kaysa sa pulitikal na pagtutol. Ang ahensya ay nagdededikasyon sa malaking bahagi ng kanilang yaman sa pagproseso ng pang-aabuso ng pulis, mga krimen ng paghihiganti, at pangangalakal ng tao — mga lugar kung saan mahalaga ang pagkakaroon ng responsibilidad. Noong 2012, 42% ng kanilang mga imbestigasyon sa karapatan ng sibil ay tumutok sa 'color of law' abuses — sobrang puwersa, maliwalaang aresto, at pagbuo ng ebidensya ng mga opisyales. Gayunpaman, may mga magkakaugnay na pagkakamali. Ang mga bagong paglabas tungkol sa NSA ay nagpapakita na ang mga ahente ng gobyerno ay gumamit ng mga instrumento ng masusing pagmamasid upang makaspi sa mga minamahal, pakinabangan ang mga pribadong tawag, at kahit na tanggalin ang mga personal na usapan dahil sa kahihiyan — hindi dahil sa protokolo. Isang dating analista ng NSA, si Adrienne Kinne, ay nag-amin na tinanggal niya ang mga rekord ng mga Amerikanong nagsasalita nang tahimik sa kanilang pamilya sa gitna ng gabi, at tinawag itong 'napakapersonal' at hindi kailangang irekord. Si King mismo, ayon sa dokumentasyon ni Pulitzer Prize-winning biographer na si David Garrow, ay napakababa-puso — hinahawakan ng serbisyo, hindi ng pagiging sikat. Ngunit ginamit ng FBI ang kanyang mga pagkakamali sa pribado, at isinalin ito sa mga armas. Ngayon, mayroon tayong mas mabuting batas, mga organong pagsusuri, at etikal na gabay — ngunit ang pagkakasala ng tao ay hindi nawawala kasama ang teknolohiya. Kapag mayroong makapangyarihang kasangkapan, at ang pagkakaroon ng responsibilidad ay nakatago sa lihim, may kakayahang ulitin ng kasaysayan. Ang tanong ay hindi lamang kung nabago natin ito — kundi kung may sapat na tapang tayong panatilihin ang pagmamasid sa mga sumasalita sa atin.

article_content: Late Tuesday night, 'Linsanity' reached new heights as Jeremy Lin delivered a clutch three-pointer with mere seconds left to secure a dramatic 90-87 victory for the New York Knicks over the Toronto Raptors. The Harvard-educated point guard finished with 27 points and 11 assists, leading his team back from a 14-point fourth-quarter deficit. Lin’s breakout performance not only extended the Knicks’ winning streak to six games but also shattered Shaquille O’Neal’s long-standing record for the most points in a player’s first five career starts—136 to O’Neal’s 129. Just days earlier, he outdueled NBA superstar Kobe Bryant, scoring 38 points in a win over the Los Angeles Lakers. After the game, Lin credited his teammates for their relentless defense and hustle. 'I just wanted to make sure I got a good shot at the end of the clock,' he told Agence France-Presse. 'Everybody was making deflections, grabbing rebounds—we clamped down. I’m thankful my coach and teammates trusted me with the ball in those final moments.' Toronto’s Jose Calderon posted 25 points, nine assists, and seven rebounds, while Knicks forward Amare Stoudemire returned from a brief personal absence to contribute 21 points and nine rebounds. The Knicks, now riding high on Lin’s momentum, face the Sacramento Kings in New York on Wednesday evening.

article_content: Cari Thomson, principal of Woodland Middle School in Washington, faced scrutiny after she handed her personal asthma inhaler to a seventh-grade student experiencing a life-threatening attack. Although she didn’t call the boy’s parents beforehand — a move that triggered their complaint — local authorities have since cleared her of any criminal wrongdoing. Woodland Police Chief Phillip Crochet stated that while her action technically broke policy, it reflected common sense and compassion, possibly preventing tragedy. Prosecuting Attorney Fred Johnson declined to press charges, agreeing her priority was saving a child’s life. Thomson herself acknowledged she violated school rules but was reassured by Superintendent Michael Green, who told her, 'It was a good thing you broke the policy.' The student’s father, Jason Birrer, admitted he believed Thomson meant well but worried the inhaler might have been too potent for his son. However, he also revealed his son had forgotten his own inhaler that day — a detail school staff say they were unaware of at the time. The situation became more complicated when two recently fired teachers, Holly Royle and Cheryl Nesbitt, submitted witness statements nearly a month after the event. Both claimed they reported the incident due to broader concerns about Thomson’s leadership, including alleged unprofessional conduct. Nesbitt delivered the statement to the Birrer family and brought them pizza — an act some interpreted as an attempt to influence them. But Nesbitt insisted it was simply a gesture of thanks, and Birrer stood by her, saying she provided valuable information and acted appropriately. School officials maintain they tried repeatedly to reach the parents before administering aid, as the school nurse was unavailable. Yet Birrer insists his wife was home and never contacted. The timing of the teachers’ reports — coming two weeks after their dismissal — has fueled speculation, though no evidence confirms retaliation. Meanwhile, a petition demanding Thomson’s removal, signed by nearly 500 people, lists serious but unrelated allegations, such as swearing at school or sharing intimate details with staff. These claims appear disconnected from the inhaler incident and may reflect a broader campaign against her rather than evidence-based grievances.

Bagaman hindi siya nagkontak muna sa mga magulang ng bata — isang galaw na nagpapagaling sa kanilang reklamo — kinlarawan siya ng mga awtoridad sa lokal na antas mula sa anumang krimen. Sinabi ni Police Chief Phillip Crochet ng Woodland na bagaman ang kanyang aksyon ay lumabag sa patakaran, ito ay nagpapakita ng karaniwang kamalayan at pagmamahal, at posibleng nag-iwas sa trahedya. Tinanggap ng Prosecuting Attorney Fred Johnson na huwag i-file ang kriminal na kasong laban sa kanya, sumasang-ayon na ang kanyang prioridad ay iligtas ang buhay ng isang bata. Kilala ni Thomson na lumabag siya sa patakaran ng paaralan ngunit pinawi ni Superintendent Michael Green ang kanyang takot, sinabi niya, 'Magandang bagay na lumabag ka sa patakaran.' Sinabi ng ama ng bata, si Jason Birrer, na naniniwala siya na may mabuting intensyon si Thomson ngunit nabahala na masyadong malakas ang inhaler para sa kanyang anak. Gayunpaman, sinabi rin niya na nakalimutan ng kanyang anak ang sarili niyang inhaler noong araw na iyon — detalye na sabi ng mga empleyado ng paaralan na hindi nila alam sa oras na iyon. Naging mas komplikado ang sitwasyon nang magbigay ng mga pahayag na saksi ang dalawang huling pinahiran na guro, sina Holly Royle at Cheryl Nesbitt, halos isang buwan matapos ang pangyayari. Parehong sinabi nila na ipinahayag nila ang insidente dahil sa mas malawak na pag-aalala tungkol sa pamumuno ni Thomson, kabilang ang mga alegasyon ng hindi propesyonal na pag-uugali. Dinala ni Nesbitt ang pahayag sa pamilya Birrer at dinala ang pizza — isang galaw na ilan ang itinuturing bilang pagsubok na mamaliw. Ngunit pinanatili ni Nesbitt na ito ay simpleng pagpapasalamat, at pinanindigan ni Birrer siya, sinabi niya na ibinigay niya ang mahalagang impormasyon at gumawa nang tama. Sinabi ng mga opisyales ng paaralan na sinubukan nilang makipag-ugnayan sa mga magulang nang maraming beses bago bigyan ang bata ng tulong, sapagkat hindi available ang nurse ng paaralan. Ngunit sinabi ni Birrer na nasa bahay ang kanyang asawa at hindi na kontakin. Ang panahon ng pagpapahayag ng mga guro — dalawang linggo matapos ang kanilang pagpapahiran — ay nagpapalakas ng spekulasyon, bagaman walang ebidensya na patotohanan ang paghihiganti. Samantala, isang petisyon na humihiling sa pag-alis kay Thomson, na may halos 500 lagda, ay listahan ang mga seryosong ngunit di nauugnay na alegasyon, tulad ng paggamit ng masasamang salita sa paaralan o pagbabahagi ng personal na aktibidad sa mga guro. Ang mga alegasyong ito ay tila hiwalay sa insidente ng inhaler at maaaring magpapakita ng mas malawak na kampanya laban sa kanya kaysa sa ebidensyal na mga pag-amin.

article_content: Last week, Sarah Sunny made history as India’s first deaf lawyer to present oral arguments in the Supreme Court—a landmark moment for accessibility in the nation’s highest judicial body. At 27, she first appeared before Chief Justice DY Chandrachud in September, when the court granted a rare exception, permitting a sign language interpreter to assist her. Just weeks later, on October 6, the court took an unprecedented step: it appointed its very own sign language interpreter for Sunny, marking the first time such a service has been formally provided in the court’s history. Justice Chandrachud emphasized the importance of inclusion, suggesting that future Constitution Bench hearings should also include interpreters so all participants can fully engage. Legal observers say this shift could transform the Indian judiciary into a more equitable space for the deaf community. Senior lawyer Menaka Guruswamy described the event as 'truly historic,' while Sanchita Ain, Sunny’s colleague, noted that her visibility will inspire countless deaf students to pursue law and push institutions toward real accessibility. Born and raised in Bengaluru, Sunny has practiced law for two years. In lower courts, she was repeatedly denied interpreters because judges doubted their understanding of legal jargon—so she submitted written arguments instead. Saurav Roychowdhury, who interpreted for her at the Supreme Court, is not a lawyer but has extensive experience translating for legal professionals, including in the Delhi High Court. Still, there are currently no certified interpreters in India trained specifically in legal terminology, making every interpretation a learning process. Sunny, who grew up with her deaf twin sister Maria and brother Pratik, credits her parents for refusing to send her to segregated schools. Instead, they fought to enroll all three children in mainstream classrooms, where she learned to lip-read and leaned on supportive classmates—even when some mocked her. She studied law at St. Joseph’s College, relying on friends and siblings for help since her mother couldn’t assist with complex legal material. After passing the bar in 2021, she began practicing. Her parents’ belief in equality, she says, gave her the courage to dream big. Meanwhile, the Delhi High Court had already set a precedent earlier this year by allowing deaf lawyer Saudamini Pethe to appear with an interpreter, prompting the court to commit to hiring its own interpreters and working with ASLI to establish standardized protocols. ASLI president Renuka Rameshan explained these measures aim to ensure clarity for both lawyers and judges. Experts are now pushing to create an official legal glossary in Indian Sign Language to standardize terminology. Roychowdhury believes this movement isn’t just about access—it’s about affirming that deaf citizens hold equal rights under the law. According to the 2011 Census, India has roughly 18 million deaf or hard-of-hearing individuals, yet fewer than 50 of the estimated 500 certified interpreters are considered truly competent and ethical. For many, like Ranjini Ramanujam, a former national-level badminton player and IT professional, the court’s decision feels like liberation. 'It’s not just a service,' she said. 'It’s a voice given back.' The Supreme Court’s move is now being seen as a model for other government offices to follow.

Sa edad na 27, una niyang lumabas bago ang Pangulo ng Korte, si Chief Justice DY Chandrachud, noong Setyembre, nang bigyan ng kahilingan ang korte na pahintulutan ang isang interpreter ng sign language upang tulungan siya. Isang ilang linggo pagkatapos, noong Oktubre 6, gumawa ang korte ng isang walang katulad na hakbang: itinuring nila ang sarili nilang interpreter ng sign language para kay Sunny, ang unang beses na ganitong serbisyo ay opisyal na ibinigay sa kasaysayan ng korte. Sinabi ni Justice Chandrachud na mahalaga ang pagkakaroon ng inklusibidad, at sinugnay na dapat magkaroon din ng interpreter sa mga darating na paghahanda ng Constitution Bench upang maunawaan ng lahat ang proseso. Sabi ng mga obserbador, maaaring baguhin ng pagbabagong ito ang sistema ng hustisya sa India upang maging mas patas para sa komunidad ng mga deaf. Tawag ni senior lawyer Menaka Guruswamy sa pangyayaring ito bilang 'totoong kasaysayan,' samantalang si Sanchita Ain, kaibigan ni Sunny, ay nagturo na ang kanyang pagkakaroon ng pagkakataon ay magpapakilala sa maraming deaf na estudyante na pumili ng karera sa batas at pilitin ang mga institusyon na maging mas accessible. Ipinanganak at lumaki sa Bengaluru, dalawang taon na ang nakalipas na nagpapratik si Sunny. Sa mga mas mababang hukuman, hindi siya pinahintulutan gamitin ang interpreter dahil sa pagdududa ng mga hukom sa kanilang kakayahang maunawaan ang mga terminolohiya sa batas—kaya nagsumite siya ng mga argumento sa pagsulat. Si Saurav Roychowdhury, na nag-interpreter para kay Sunny sa Supreme Court, ay hindi abogado ngunit may malawak na karanasan sa pagpapalit ng salita para sa mga propesyonal sa batas, kabilang ang dalawang kaso sa Delhi High Court. Gayunpaman, wala pa ring sertipikadong interpreter sa India na tinuruan nang espesipiko sa legal terminology, kaya bawat pagpapalit ay isang patuloy na proseso. Si Sunny, na lumaki kasama ang kanyang deaf na twin na si Maria at kanyang kapatid na si Pratik, ay nagpapasalamat sa kanyang mga magulang dahil sa pagtutol nila na ipasa siya sa mga espesyal na paaralan. Sa halip, ipinaglaban nila ang pagpapakilala sa kanilang tatlong anak sa mga pangkalahatang klase, kung saan natutunan niya ang lip reading at sumuporta sa kanyang mga kaibigan—kahit na mayroong nagtatawa sa kanya. Nag-aral siya ng batas sa St. Joseph’s College, nakikipag-ugnayan sa mga kaibigan at kapatid para sa tulong dahil hindi na makatulong ang kanyang ina sa mga kumplikadong materyales sa batas. Pagkatapos makapasa sa bar exam noong 2021, nagsimula siya sa pagpapratik. Ang paniniwala ng kanyang mga magulang sa pantay-pantay na pagtrato, sabi niya, ang nagbigay sa kanya ng tiwala na sundin ang kanyang mga pangarap. Samantala, ang Delhi High Court ay nagsagawa na ng isang prekedyente noong nakaraang buwan nang pahintulutan ang deaf na abogadong si Saudamini Pethe na lumabas kasama ang interpreter, na nagresulta sa pagpapasya ng korte na mag-apoint ng sarili nilang interpreters at magtrabaho kasama ang ASLI upang magbuo ng mga istandar na protokolo. Sinabi ni Renuka Rameshan, pangulo ng ASLI, na ang layunin ng mga hakbang na ito ay siguraduhin ang pag-unawa ng mga abogado at hukom. Kasalukuyang tinutulungan ng mga eksperto na likhain ang opisyal na legal na talahanayan sa Indian Sign Language upang mai-standardize ang terminolohiya. Sabi ni Roychowdhury, ang kilos na ito ay hindi lamang tungkol sa access—kundi tungkol sa pagpapatibay na ang mga deaf ay may pantay na karapatan sa ilalim ng batas. Ayon sa 2011 Census, mayroong halos 18 milyong mga deaf o may mahirap marinig sa India, ngunit mas kaunti sa 50 sa mga 500 na sertipikadong interpreter ang itinuturing na tunay na kwalipikado at etikal. Para sa marami, tulad ni Ranjini Ramanujam, isang dating national-level badminton player at IT professional, ang desisyon ng korte ay parang kalayaan. 'Hindi ito simpleng serbisyo,' sabi niya. 'Ito ay ibinigay na boses.' Ang pagkilos ng Supreme Court ay ngayon ay itinuturing na modelo para sa iba pang ahensya ng gobyerno na sundin.

article_content: Nutrient use on United States golf courses increases management costs and has the potential to influence ecosystems. Therefore, assessing nutrient use and management practices is critical to developing and teaching best management practices. The objectives of this survey were to measure nutrient use and management practices on United States golf courses in 2021 and to determine whether changes had occurred since 2006. A survey was created to allow comparisons across years. Respondents were asked to provide nutrient data based on the guaranteed analysis listed on fertilizer labels. The instrument was distributed in English via online software (Qualtrics, Provo, UT). A survey link was emailed to golf facilities using mailing lists from the National Golf Foundation (Jupiter, FL) and the Golf Course Superintendents Association of America (Lawrence, KS), resulting in the link being sent to 14,033 unique golf facilities. Additionally, the survey and link were promoted on social media by staff of the Golf Course Superintendents Association of America. The survey remained open for seven consecutive weeks, beginning on April 1, 2022. Responses were received from 1,444 facilities, representing 10.3% of the known total number of U.S. golf facilities, defined as having at least one golf course. From 2006 to 2021, projected tons of nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P2O5), and soluble potash (K2O) applied to U.S. golf facilities declined by 41%, 59%, and 54%, respectively. This decline was likely due to golf facility closures, reduced fertilized acreage, and lower nutrient application rates. Nutrient restrictions likely influenced the amount of P2O5 applied. The percentage of golf facilities that did not apply P2O5 or K2O increased from 2006 to 2021. Although the percentage of golf facilities conducting soil tests declined from 2006 to 2021, soil testing continues to raise concerns: facilities that conducted soil tests applied more nutrients than those that did not. Although soil testing is often framed as a conservation practice, the finding that it was associated with higher N, P2O5, and K2O application rates suggests otherwise. Therefore, greater emphasis should be placed on the core principles of proper soil testing — including sampling, testing, interpretation, and recommendation. Nearly half of U.S. golf facilities used the saturated paste soil extractant for phosphorus analysis, a method not endorsed by turfgrass soil scientists. The most important factors used in nutrient application decisions remained consistent with prior years: visual observations, weather conditions, and previous product performance. Golf course superintendents appear to prioritize nutrient management, as shown by reductions in both fertilized acreage and application rates on operational facilities. Dr. Shaddox is an assistant professor at the University of Kentucky. His research focuses on soil fertility and turfgrass nutrition, with an emphasis on reducing costs and environmental risks from granular and foliar nutrient applications. He also develops reliable interpretations of soil and tissue tests for turfgrasses. The study was published in the journal HortTechnology.
translated_content: Ang paggamit ng mga nutrisyon sa mga golf course sa Estados Unidos ay nagdudulot ng pagtaas sa gastos sa pamamahala at may potensyal na makaapekto sa mga ecosystem. Kaya mahalaga ang pagsusuri sa paggamit at pamamahala ng nutrisyon upang magbuo at magturo ng pinakamabuting pamamaraan. Ang layunin ng survey na ito ay sukatin ang paggamit ng nutrisyon at mga pamamaraan sa pamamahala sa mga golf course sa Estados Unidos noong 2021 at tukuyin kung may pagbabago na nangyari mula 2006. Isang survey ang nilikha upang mapaghambing ang mga sagot sa iba't ibang taon. Hiningi sa mga sumagot na ibigay ang datos tungkol sa nutrisyon batay sa guaranteed analysis na nakalista sa mga label ng abono. Ang instrumento ay na-distribute sa Ingles gamit ang online software (Qualtrics, Provo, UT). Isang link sa survey ay na-email sa mga golf facility gamit ang mailing list ng National Golf Foundation (Jupiter, FL) at ang Golf Course Superintendents Association of America (Lawrence, KS), na nagresulta sa pagpapadala ng link sa 14,033 natatanging golf facility. Dagdag pa rito, ipinromosyon ng mga miyembro ng Golf Course Superintendents Association of America ang survey at ang link sa social media. Ang survey ay magagamit para sa pagkumpleto sa loob ng pitong magkakasunod na linggo, mula Abril 1, 2022. Natanggap ang mga sagot mula sa 1,444 na facility, na kumakatawan sa 10.3% ng kabuuang bilang ng kilalang golf facility sa Estados Unidos, na tinukoy bilang may kahit isang golf course. Mula 2006 hanggang 2021, bumaba ang inaasahang tonelada ng nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P2O5), at soluble potash (K2O) na ginamit sa mga golf facility sa Estados Unidos ng 41%, 59%, at 54%, ayon sa pagkakasunod-sunod. Ang pagbaba ay malamang dahil sa pagkakasara ng golf facility, pagbawas sa sukat ng lupaing pinapabango, at pagbawas sa rate ng nutrisyon. Posibleng naimpluwensiya ng mga limitasyon sa nutrisyon ang dami ng P2O5 na ginamit. Dumami ang porsiyento ng mga golf facility na hindi gumamit ng P2O5 o K2O mula 2006 hanggang 2021. Bagaman bumaba ang porsiyento ng mga golf facility na gumagawa ng soil test mula 2006 hanggang 2021, patuloy pa ring isyu ang paggamit ng soil test: mas maraming nutrisyon ang ginamit ng mga facility na gumawa ng soil test kaysa sa mga hindi. Bagaman madalas ituring na isang praktis na pangkonservasyon ang soil testing, ang natuklasan na kasali ito sa pagtaas ng paggamit ng N, P2O5, at K2O ay nagmumungkahi ng kabaligtaran. Kaya, dapat bigyan ng mas malaking diin ang mga pangunahing prinsipyo ng tamang soil testing — kabilang ang pagkuha ng sample, pagsubok, pag-interpret, at pag-rekomenda. Halos kalahati ng mga golf facility sa Estados Unidos ay gumamit ng saturated paste soil extractant para sa pagsusuri ng phosphorus sa lupa, isang paraan na hindi inirerekomenda ng mga siyentipiko sa lupa at turfgrass. Ang pinakamahalagang mga salik na ginamit sa paggawa ng desisyon sa paggamit ng nutrisyon ay nanatiling pareho na sa nakaraang taon: mga paningin, kondisyon ng panahon, at dating performans ng produkto. Maaaring unahin ng mga golf course superintendent ang pamamahala ng nutrisyon, gaya ng ipinapakita ng pagbaba sa sukat ng lupaing pinapabango at sa rate ng paggamit ng nutrisyon sa mga operasyonal na facility. Si Dr. Shaddox ay isang assistant professor sa University of Kentucky. Ang kanyang programa sa pananaliksik ay tumutok sa soil fertility at turfgrass nutrition, na may pansin sa pagbawas ng gastos at panganib sa kalikasan mula sa paggamit ng granular at foliar nutrients. Patuloy niyang inaangkop ang mga tiyak na interpretasyon ng soil at tissue tests para sa turfgrasses. Ipinublished ang pag-aaral sa journal na HortTechnology.

article_content: For millions of Americans out of work, unemployment insurance isn’t just a benefit — it’s the difference between keeping the lights on and losing everything. But right now, that safety net is being dismantled, even as job opportunities remain painfully scarce. Since February, more than 400,000 people in 25 states have already lost access to federal extended benefits, which offered a final few months of support to those who’d been jobless the longest. By September, that number will climb to half a million across 35 states. Meanwhile, another major program — Emergency Unemployment Compensation — helping 2.6 million people with up to 53 weeks of aid — is set to shrink drastically starting this June. Workers in 24 states will feel the blow immediately, and those who lose their jobs after July may find zero federal assistance left by year’s end. What makes this crisis so devastating is how long people have been unemployed. Of the 12.7 million Americans without jobs, over 5 million have been searching for work for six months or longer. One in three have been out for more than a year. The average person is now unemployed for nearly ten months — far beyond the typical six-month state benefit window. Back in 2009, Congress stepped in with emergency measures that extended aid up to 99 weeks in the hardest-hit areas. Those measures were never meant to be permanent, but they were necessary — because this wasn’t a normal recession. The recovery has been sluggish, and the job market hasn’t caught up. Yet instead of expanding support, lawmakers are pulling back. Critics say extended benefits discourage people from working, but that’s a myth rooted in stigma, not data. Research consistently shows unemployment insurance helps people stay connected to the workforce — it doesn’t trap them. Living on $300 a week isn’t luxury; it’s survival. And when you cut those checks, you don’t just hurt individuals — you hurt entire communities. Families face eviction, hunger, and debt. Local economies lose spending power. This isn’t fiscal responsibility — it’s economic self-sabotage. If we truly want recovery, we need bold action: targeted job creation for the long-term unemployed, laws banning discrimination against job seekers based on their unemployment status, and a commitment to keep basic income support alive until the job market improves. Right now, fewer than half of the unemployed receive any aid — and that number is falling fast. We can’t call ourselves a nation that values dignity if we abandon those who’ve tried everything and still can’t find work. Congress must act before the last thread of federal unemployment insurance vanishes at the end of the year.

Ngunit ngayon, ang seguridad na ito ay tinatanggal, kahit na ang mga pagkakataon sa trabaho ay nananatiling malalim na kakaunti. Mula pebrero, mas higit sa 400,000 tao sa 25 estado ay nawalan na ng akses sa pambansang extended benefits, na nagbigay ng ilang buwan pang suporta sa pinakamahabang panahong walang trabaho. Samantala, isa pang pangunahing programa — Emergency Unemployment Compensation — na tumutulong sa 2.6 milyong tao na may hanggang 53 linggo ng benepisyo — ay lalakiin nang malaki simula sa Hunyo. Ang mga manggagawa sa 24 estado ay makararanas ng agad na epekto, at ang mga taong nawawalan ng trabaho pagkatapos ng Hulyo ay maaaring walang anumang pambansang tulong sa dulo ng taon. Ang nagiging dahilan kung bakit ito'y sobrang nakakalungkot ay ang tagal ng panahon na walang trabaho ang mga tao. Sa 12.7 milyong Amerikano na walang trabaho, higit sa 5 milyon ang naghahanap ng trabaho na nanganganak na ng anim na buwan o higit pa. Isang kada tatlo ay wala sa trabaho nang higit sa isang taon. Ang karaniwang tao ay ngayon ay walang trabaho nang halos sampung buwan — mas mahaba kaysa sa karaniwang anim na buwan na benepisyo ng estado. Noong 2009, gumawa ang Kongreso ng emergency measures na nagpalawak ng tulong hanggang 99 linggo sa pinakamalalaking naapektuhang estado. Hindi ito dapat magtagal, ngunit kinakailangan ito — dahil hindi ito karaniwang recession. Ang pagbabalik ay mabagal, at ang merkado sa trabaho ay hindi pa nakakasabay. Ngunit sa halip na palakasin ang suporta, ang mga politiko ay umuwi. Sinasabi ng mga kalaban na ang extended benefits ay nagpapahaba sa pagiging walang trabaho, ngunit ito ay isang mito na batay sa stigma, hindi sa datos. Patuloy na ipinapakita ng pananaliksik na tumutulong ang unemployment insurance sa pagpanatili ng ugnayan ng mga manggagawa sa puwersa ng trabaho — hindi ito nagtatago sa kanila. Ang pamumuhay sa $300 kada linggo ay hindi luxury; ito ay pagpapanatili. At kapag tinanggal mo ang mga tseke na ito, hindi mo lang nasasaktan ang mga indibidwal — sinasaktan mo ang buong komunidad. Ang mga pamilya ay nakakaranas ng pagpapalabas, gutom, at utang. Nawawala ang kapangyarihan sa pagkonsumo sa lokal na ekonomiya. Ito ay hindi responsableng pampublikong patakaran — ito ay sariling pagpapahirap sa ekonomiya. Kung talagang nais natin ang pagbabalik, kailangan nating gawin ang malalaking hakbang: target na mga programa sa paglikha ng trabaho para sa pinakamahabang panahong walang trabaho, batas na bawal ang diskriminasyon laban sa mga naghahanap ng trabaho batay sa kanilang pagiging walang trabaho, at pagpapanatili ng pangunahing suporta sa kita hanggang sa mabuti na ang merkado sa trabaho. Sa kasalukuyan, mas kaunti sa kalahati ng mga walang trabaho ang natatanggap ng anumang tulong — at bumababa ito nang mabilis. Hindi natin pwedeng tawaging bansang may dangal kung iiwan natin ang mga taong nagsubok ng lahat pero hindi pa rin nakakahanap ng trabaho. Kailangan ng Kongreso na gumawa bago nawala ang huling tulong sa federal unemployment insurance sa dulo ng taon.

article_content: Ottawa, Canada (CNN) — It was unexpected — even for a journalist — to be driving down Wellington Street, the city’s ceremonial boulevard, and suddenly find myself caught in the chaos of a disaster. I was rushing to a TV studio at mid-morning when I passed the National War Memorial, mere minutes after a soldier had been shot. Police were shutting down streets, halting traffic, shouting orders, machine guns raised, fingers on triggers. Within moments, a citywide lockdown was enforced — lasting until late afternoon. It was from this confinement that I began writing this. This is not supposed to happen in Canada — not in Ottawa, its quiet, self-contained capital. Sentinels do not fall on duty at the National War Memorial during our season of remembrance. Politicians do not huddle in committee rooms while gunfire echoes through Parliament’s Gothic halls. Sharpshooters do not perch on copper rooftops, scanning for men with long rifles. This is Canada — once called the 'Peaceable Kingdom.' But now, like so many nations, we’ve learned the harsh truth of the 21st century: It can happen here. When a gunman killed a lone soldier at the memorial — and then, possibly with accomplices (still unknown), stormed Parliament’s front doors and opened fire — something shifted. When hundreds of MPs barricaded themselves behind desks and chairs, trapped inside their offices, something changed. When the city center locked down and a perimeter sealed off the parliamentary zone, confining thousands in offices and shops, something changed. It’s tempting to say, as many will, that Canada lost its innocence today. But Canada was never truly innocent. A nation that sent 100,000 of its young men to die in two world wars knows sacrifice. Especially now, as Canadians wear red poppies until Remembrance Day on November 11. What we can say is this: Canada has lost its ignorance — and perhaps, its complacency. We now understand, chillingly, that evil can strike even here, in the heart of our democracy. Many of us assumed it couldn’t — wouldn’t — happen. In 147 years as a democracy, we’ve never faced revolution, civil war, or foreign invasion. Abroad, we’ve never waged conquests, held colonies, or fought alone. For decades, we led the world as peacekeepers, exporting the compromise we live by at home. We are an open, diverse society with some of the highest immigration rates globally. Perhaps we believed ourselves untouched by the pathologies and hatreds of others. Not here. Not us. But why should Canada be exempt? Canadians served in Afghanistan. We are NATO members. We are allies of the United States. Just weeks ago, Parliament voted to join airstrikes against the Islamic State in Iraq. Our jets will soon fly. We shouldn’t be surprised. Warning signs were there: a foiled plot years ago to bomb Parliament and behead the Prime Minister. Recent reports show growing numbers of Canadian Muslims joining jihadist ranks overseas. Whether this was a coordinated terror attack or the act of a lone extremist fueled by ideology, it’s another stark reminder: success, openness, and global engagement carry risks. Unlike the U.S., Canada has minimal violent crime. It remains among the safest industrialized nations. Murders — even mass shootings — occur rarely in Toronto, Montreal, or Vancouver. Ottawa, Canada’s fourth-largest city, is a government town — like Canberra or Sacramento — not London or Paris. Its mayor considers light rail a bold innovation, years after other cities built theirs. So yes, it’s shocking, terrifying, and heartbreaking that this happened here — of all places. But it was naive to believe a country of 35 million people, actively engaged in a war overseas, would never face such violence. It has. Our long, sweet season of ignorance is over.

Nagmamadali ako patungo sa isang TV studio noong tanghali nang makita ko ang National War Memorial, ilang minuto lamang pagkatapos ma-shoot ang isang sundalo. Ang pulis ay nagpaputol ng mga kalsada, nag-iistopo ng trapiko, nag-uutos nang malakas, may mga machine gun na inilalabas, ang mga daliri sa trigger. Hindi dapat mamatay ang mga bantay sa kanilang tungkulin sa National War Memorial sa panahon ng aming panahon ng pagsaulo. Hindi dapat magtago ang mga politiko sa mga kuwarto ng komite habang tumitigil ang baril sa mga pasilyo ng Gothic ng Parliament. Hindi dapat magpahinga ang mga sharpshooter sa mga bubong ng tanso, hinahanap ang mga lalaki na may mahabang baril. Ito ay Canada — dating tinatawag na 'Peaceable Kingdom.' Ngunit ngayon, tulad ng maraming bansa, natutunan natin ang matinding katotohanan ng ika-21 siglo: Maaari itong mangyari rito. Nang ma-shoot ng isang tao ang isang mag-isa mong sundalo sa memorial — at pagkatapos, posibleng kasama ang mga kasamahan (hindi pa alam kung sino o gaano karami) — pumasok sa harap na pinto ng Parliament ng Canada at nagsimulang magbunsod, nangyari ang isang pagbabago. Nang isara ang sentro ng lungsod at itayo ang isang perimeter paligid sa parliamentary zone, nakakulong ang libo-libong tao sa kanilang mga opisina at tindahan, nangyari ang isang pagbabago. Masyadong karaniwan ang sabihin — gaya ng maraming gagawin — na nawala na ang kabanalan ng Canada ngayon. Pero hindi totoo na walang sala ang Canada; isang bansa na nagpadala ng 100,000 ng kanyang mga kabataan para mamatay sa dalawang digmaan sa mundo ay kilala ang paghihiganti. Lalo na ngayon, habang isinasuot ng mga Canadian ang mga pulang poppy hanggang sa Remembrance Day sa Nobyembre 11. Ano ang pwede nating sabihin ay ito: Nawala na ang kawalan ng kaalaman ng Canada — at posibleng bahagi rin ng kanyang komplasidad. Ngayon naiintindihan natin, nang hiyawan, na maaaring dumating ang kasamaan kahit dito, sa puso ng ating demokrasya. Marami sa atin ay naniniwala na hindi ito maaaring mangyari — hindi ito mangyayari. Sa 147 taon bilang demokrasya, hindi natin napagdaanan ang isang rebolusyon, sibil na digmaan, o pananakop. Sa labas, hindi natin pinagsikapan ang mga digmaan ng pagpapalawak, hindi natin pinanatili ang mga kolonya, at hindi natin ipinaglaban ang sarili natin. Sa maraming taon, aming pinuno ang mundo bilang mga tagapagpanatili ng kapayapaan, ipinapakita ang kompromiso na ginagawa natin sa bahay. Kami ay isang bukas, maingat na lipunan na may isa sa pinakamataas na antas ng imigrasyon sa mundo. Baka naisip natin na hindi tayo mapapagod ng mga kakaibang sakit at prehensiyon mula sa loob o labas. Hindi dito. Hindi kami. Ngunit bakit dapat maging immune ang Canada? Nakipaglaban ang mga Canadian sa Afghanistan. Kami ay miyembro ng NATO at isang matandang kaalyado ng Estados Unidos. Noong ilang linggo ang nakalipas, bumoto ang ating Parliament upang sumali sa kampanya sa hangin laban sa Islamic State sa Iraq. Sa susunod na linggo, pupunta ang aming eroplano doon. Hindi dapat tayo magulat. May mga palatandaan na nandito: isang plot na nabigo noong ilang taon ang nakalipas na mag-bomba sa Parliament at magpatay ng Punong Ministro. Mas maraming ulat ngayon tungkol sa 'radikalized' na mga Muslim na Canadian na sumali sa mga jihadista sa Middle East. Kung ano man ang nangyari rito — isang organisadong terorista o gawa ng isang mag-isa na pinagpapalakas ng relihiyon o ideolohiya — ito ay isang iba pang paalala sa mga panganib na laging dumidikit sa isang tagumpay na kahit na kumplikadong lipunan na naghahangad na magkaroon ng lugar sa mundo. Sa pagkakaiba sa Estados Unidos, mababa ang krimen sa Canada. Isa ito sa pinakaligtas na industriyalisadong bansa. Ang mga pagpatay — kahit mga mass killing — ay rare sa Toronto, Montreal, at Vancouver. Ang Ottawa, ang ikaapat na pinakamalaking lungsod ng Canada, ay isang lungsod ng pamahalaan — tulad ng Canberra o Sacramento — hindi London, Paris, o Rome. Ang punong bayan nito ay itinuturing na ang pagpalit ng isang masiraan na pampublikong aklatan o pagtatayo ng light rail — taon na ang nakalipas kaysa sa iba pang mga lungsod sa Canada — ay isang malakas na ideya. Kaya, nakakagulat, nakakatakot, at nakakalungkot na ito ay nangyari dito — ng lahat ng lugar. Pero mali ang paniniwala na isang bansa ng 35 milyong tao, aktibong nakikilahok sa digmaan sa labas, ay hindi maaaring harapin ang ganitong karahasan. Narito na. Nawala na ang aming mahaba't matamis na panahon ng kawalan ng kaalaman.

article_content: Although the UK Ministry of Defence publicly insists it has no plans to move Britain’s nuclear-armed submarines from their current base in Faslane, Scotland, internal discussions are underway to explore relocating them to Wales — specifically to the deep-water port of Milford Haven in Pembrokeshire. This contingency planning comes amid rising political pressure from the Scottish National Party (SNP), which is poised to win a large number of seats in the upcoming general election and could become the decisive force in forming a future government. SNP leader Nicola Sturgeon has stated that removing the Trident nuclear deterrent from Scottish soil is non-negotiable if her party enters any power-sharing arrangement with Labour. Meanwhile, Welsh First Minister Carwyn Jones has signaled openness to hosting the fleet, noting that Milford Haven offers ideal geographic advantages. The MoD maintains that Faslane remains the only operational base for the UK’s continuous at-sea deterrent and that no formal relocation plans exist. Yet, insiders say preparing for all eventualities is prudent, especially given the SNP’s surging popularity. Polls show that while a majority of Scots favor abolishing nuclear weapons, only a quarter of the wider UK public agrees. In a separate but unrelated development, rumors surfaced about British Tornado jets possibly returning to Afghanistan to conduct airstrikes following recent Taliban offensives. However, the Ministry of Defence has firmly dismissed these claims, reiterating that no combat aircraft deployments to Afghanistan are planned or under consideration.

Ang paghahanda para sa ganitong kahilingan ay nangyayari habang tumataas ang presyur mula sa Scottish National Party (SNP), na nasa posisyon na manalo ng maraming mga puwesto sa darating na halalan at maaaring maging desisyong puwersa sa pagbuo ng hinaharap na gobyerno. Ang pangulo ng SNP, si Nicola Sturgeon, ay nagsabi na ang pag-alis ng Trident nuclear deterrent mula sa lupaing Skotlond ay hindi kompromiso kung ang kanyang partido ay makakasali sa anumang kasunduang pagbabahagi ng kapangyarihan sa Labour. Samantala, ang Punong Ministro ng Wales, si Carwyn Jones, ay nagpahiwatig ng pagtanggap sa pagtatayo ng barko, at sinabi na ang Milford Haven ay may mga ideyal na katangian sa heograpiko. Pinapanatili ng MoD na ang Faslane ay ang tanging operasyonal na base para sa patuloy na deterrante sa dagat ng UK, at wala pang opisyal na plano ng paglipat. Gayunpaman, sabi ng mga pinagkakatiwalaan, mahalaga ang paghahanda para sa lahat ng posibilidad, lalo na dahil sa pagtaas ng populartiy ng SNP. Ayon sa mga survey, habang ang karamihan sa mga Skot ay sumusuporta sa pagtatanggal ng nuclear weapons, lamang ang 25% ng mga botante sa buong UK ang nagsasabing dapat alisin ang Trident. Sa isang magkakaibang pero di-nakakaugnay na pag-unlad, lumabas ang mga alalahanin tungkol sa posibleng pagbabalik ng mga British Tornado jets sa Afghanistan upang gawin ang mga pag-atake susunod sa mga kamakailang pag-atake ng Taliban. Gayunpaman, tinanggihan nang matigas ng Ministry of Defence ang mga reklamo, at binigyang-diin na wala pang plano o aktwal na paghahanda para sa anumang pagpapadala ng mga eroplano sa Afghanistan.

article_content: More than 11,000 children have been killed in Syria’s civil war, with summary executions and torture alarmingly common, according to a major report by the London-based Oxford Research Group (ORG). The study, titled 'Stolen Futures: The hidden toll of child casualties in Syria,' documents 11,420 child deaths — including those killed in crossfire, by sniper fire, execution, or torture. Of these, 70% died from explosions, and 25% from small arms fire. Among the dead, 764 children were recorded as summarily executed, and 112 were tortured — some as young as infants. Older boys between 13 and 17 were the most frequent targets of deliberate attacks. Aleppo recorded the highest number of child fatalities, but Daraa suffered the highest rate relative to population — roughly one child in every 400 was killed. On August 21, 2013, 128 children lost their lives in the chemical weapons attack on Ghouta. Co-author Hamit Dardagan stated, 'The data shows bombs and bullets ended the lives of over 10,000 Syrian children in just 30 months of war. The world must pay closer attention to the impact on children.' Hana Salama, another co-author, emphasized the brutality: 'Children are bombed in their homes, shot while waiting in bread lines, tortured, and gassed. All parties to the conflict must protect children and pursue peace.' The report concludes that explosive weapons must never be used in areas where children live and learn, and that lasting peace — not more violence — is the only path to securing their future.

Ang pag-aaral, na may pamagat na 'Stolen Futures: Ang nakatago na halaga ng mga biktima na bata sa Syria,' ay nagtatala ng 11,420 kamatayan ng mga bata — kabilang ang mga namatay sa pagkabigay, pagbubunot, pagkakasuhan, o pagmamalupit. Sa mga ito, 70% ay namatay dahil sa pagsabog, at 25% dahil sa mga maliit na armas. Sa mga nasawi, 764 ang bata na itinatala bilang pinagsuhan nang walang paglilitis, at 112 ay pinagmamalupit — ilan ay ganap na mga batang-bata. Ang mga lalaking bata na nasa edad na 13 hanggang 17 ang pinaka-karaniwang biktima ng mga pinauunlad na pag-atake. Ang Aleppo ang may pinakamataas na bilang ng mga kamatayan ng mga bata, ngunit ang Daraa ang may pinakamataas na antas relativo sa populasyon — halos isang bata sa bawat 400 ang namatay. Noong Agosto 21, 2013, 128 ang mga bata na namatay sa pag-atake gamit ang kemikal na sandata sa Ghouta. Ang tagapagsulat na si Hamit Dardagan ay nagsabi, 'Ang datos ay nagpapakita na ang mga bomba at bala ay nagwakas sa buhay ng higit sa 10,000 na mga bata sa Syria sa loob lamang ng 30 buwan ng digmaan. Lahat ng panig sa konflikto ay dapat protektahan ang mga bata at hanapin ang kapayapaan.' Ang ulat ay nagtatapos na ang mga eksplodyong sandata ay hindi dapat gamitin sa mga lugar kung saan naninirahan at naglalaro ang mga bata, at ang matatag na kapayapaan — hindi pa higit pang karahasan — ang tanging paraan upang jaminin ang kaligtasan nila.

article_content: In the chaotic aftermath of a deadly attack on Canada’s Parliament, Sergeant-at-Arms Kevin Vickers calmly walked through the halls, gun in hand, having just ended the threat posed by Michael Zehaf-Bibeau. The 58-year-old former RCMP officer, who had served as head of parliamentary security since 2005, had never fired his weapon in the line of duty—until that Wednesday morning. Zehaf-Bibeau, a 32-year-old man who had converted to Islam, first shot and killed Corporal Nathan Cirillo, a 24-year-old reservist on ceremonial guard duty at the National War Memorial. He then stormed into the House of Commons, sparking a frantic chase. Vickers, armed with his service pistol and known for his physical fitness, led the response. Multiple shots rang out inside the chamber, and Zehaf-Bibeau was killed. Video captured the tense moments as officers rushed toward the attacker, with Vickers at the front. The entire ordeal lasted mere minutes. The next day, Vickers returned to work, receiving a standing ovation from MPs. He quietly acknowledged the applause, later issuing a statement honoring Cirillo and expressing hope for the recovery of Constable Samearn Son, who was wounded in the leg. Meanwhile, Zehaf-Bibeau’s parents released a tearful public message, apologizing for the pain their son caused, admitting they didn’t understand him, and asking for privacy. Prime Minister Stephen Harper and Queen Elizabeth II both condemned the violence, affirming Canada’s strength in the face of terror. Across the country, flags flew at half-mast as Ottawa grappled with the shock. An unrelated man was briefly detained for crossing crime tape near the memorial site. The incident underscored the quiet preparedness of public servants—and the devastating cost of senseless violence.

article_content: A fire that destroyed one building of the Quba Islamic Institute in Houston is believed to have been set intentionally. Authorities say an accelerant was used in the 5 a.m. fire on Friday, according to Ahsan Zahid, the 25-year-old son of one of the imams. Zahid said an investigator informed him the incident was suspected arson and not an accident. The Houston Fire Department is still investigating the cause and has not yet confirmed it. The FBI stated Saturday it is monitoring the situation and may take a more active role, according to Reuters. The Council on American Islamic Relations’ Texas office has urged investigators to examine possible hate crime motivations. Federal agencies are expected to increase involvement if hate crime charges are pursued. No injuries were reported. The fire, which primarily consumed a storage building, caused approximately $100,000 in damage. The structure housed computers, lighting, and equipment intended for renovations. The Quba Islamic Institute serves as a prayer space, hosts community events, offers Arabic classes, and runs a Sunday School. Despite the fire, all programs—including a scheduled talk by former Guantanamo Bay guard and Muslim convert Terry Holdbrooks—continued as planned. Zahid told Daily Mail Online that the institute had raised $2,500 in donations as of Saturday afternoon via qubahouston.org. In the days leading up to the fire, two suspicious incidents occurred: a man drove past the building and mockingly shouted 'Allah,' and another individual with a covered face was chased away from the premises. The institute’s Facebook page was flooded with anti-Muslim comments following posts about the fire. In response, the center thanked commenters for their perspectives and urged tolerance. This incident follows the deaths of three Muslim students—Deah Shaddy Barakat, 23; his wife, Yusor Mohammad Abu-Salha, 21; and her sister, Razan Mohammad Abu-Salha, 19—in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, which federal authorities are investigating as a potential hate crime. Texas has the eighth-largest Muslim population in the U.S., according to the Texas State Historical Association. Last month, the annual Texas Muslim Capitol Day in Austin was targeted by anti-Islam protesters. In 2011, the Houston Fire Department confirmed a deliberate fire at another mosque in the city.

Ang sunog, na pangunahing nagbaha sa isang storage building, ay nagdulot ng halos $100,000 na pinsala. Ang gusali ay nagtatago ng mga computer, ilaw, at kagamitan para sa pagrereparo. Ang Quba Islamic Institute ay isang lugar para sa panalangin, nagtatampok ng mga komunidad, nagtataguyod ng mga klase sa Arabe, at may Sunday School. Sa kabila ng sunog, patuloy pa rin ang lahat ng programa—kabilang ang isang inadwisadong talakayan ni Terry Holdbrooks, dating guwardiya ng Guantanamo Bay at nagkonbertir sa Islam. Sa mga araw bago ang sunog, dalawa ang mga kakaibang pangyayari: isang lalaki ay dumadaan sa gusali at sumigaw nang mapapahiya ng 'Allah,' at isa pang tao na may takip sa mukha ay tinaboy mula sa lugar. Sumunod sa insidenteng ito ang pagkamatay ng tatlong Muslim na estudyante—Deah Shaddy Barakat, 23; ang asawa niya, Yusor Mohammad Abu-Salha, 21; at ang kapatid niya, Razan Mohammad Abu-Salha, 19—sa Chapel Hill, North Carolina, na sinusuri ng mga pambansang awtoridad bilang posibleng krimen dahil sa pagkakaiba-iba. article_content: In the early hours of a bank holiday morning in Spondon, Derbyshire, a stolen three-tonne flatbed lorry was used to repeatedly smash into the front of a semi-detached home, leaving the structure dangerously unstable. The house, valued at £120,000, was unoccupied at the time, and thankfully no one was injured. Residents nearby described the impacts as deafening—comparing them to earthquakes or explosions—as the vehicle struck the building at least three times before speedily departing. Two individuals, dressed in balaclavas, were seen exiting the lorry and fleeing on foot, later joining a waiting white van. Neighbors, shaken and fearful that the house might collapse, were urgently evacuated. One resident, Kay Nyakale, recounted how the ground shook for several seconds after each collision, and another, Anne Byrne, recalled hearing shouts and seeing figures near the truck before the crashes. An anonymous eyewitness reported that a taxi driver initially refused to stop, overwhelmed by the chaos, until the lorry hit the house with a thunderous roar. After the impacts, several masked figures emerged from the house empty-handed, then disappeared into the getaway vehicle. Police confirmed the lorry had been stolen from a waste company in Staffordshire and have launched a full-scale manhunt. While no weapons were involved, authorities believe the attack may stem from a long-standing local conflict. No arrests have yet been made, and investigators are urging anyone with information to come forward.

Ang bahay, na may halaga na £120,000, ay walang tao sa loob sa panahon ng insidente, at naiwasan ang anumang pinsala sa katawan. Ang mga kapitbahay ay nagsalita ng malakas na ingay—kumukumpara sa mga lindol o pagsabog—habang tinamaan ng sasakyan ang gusali ng hindi bababa sa tatlong beses bago mabilis na umalis. Dalawang indibidwal, nakasuot ng balaclava, ay nakita na lumabas sa lorry at tumakas nang magmaliw, at sumama sa isang nakaantay na puting van. Ang mga kapitbahay, na nakakatakot at natatakot na maaaring mabagsak ang bahay, ay agad na pinag-iiwanan. Isang residente, si Kay Nyakale, ay nagkuwento kung paano gumalaw ang lupa ng ilang segundo pagkatapos ng bawat tama, at ang isa pang residente, si Anne Byrne, ay naalala ang pagkikisig at pagkakita ng mga tao malapit sa trak bago ang mga pagtama. Isang anonymous na saksi ay nagraport na ang isang taxista ay una'y tumanggi na tumigil, na sobrang nabigla sa gulat, hanggang sa saktan ng lorry ang bahay nang malakas na ingay. Pagkatapos ng mga pagtama, ilang nakakapalayaw na tao ang lumabas sa bahay nang walang anuman, at pagkatapos ay nawala sa isang getaway car. Tiniyak ng pulisya na ang lorry ay nakuha mula sa isang kompanya ng basura sa Staffordshire at sinimulan ang isang malawakang paghahanap. Habang walang armas ang ginamit, naniniwala ang awtoridad na maaaring mula sa isang matagal nang lokal na away ang pag-atake. Walang arestado pa, at hinihingi ng mga imbestigador ang anumang impormasyon mula sa mga saksi.

article_content: Philadelphia (CNN) — Robert Sanabria never thought he’d see his older brother again. He was 15 when Edwin, then 18, left home. Born prematurely with only one functioning lung, Edwin spent his school years in special education. Robert remembers him as quiet, humble, and deeply kind. 'When he left, he just took off,' Robert told CNN last Saturday. 'He was in love—and ran away.' He last saw Edwin in 1999. Neighbors occasionally claimed they spotted Edwin around Philadelphia. 'It was like a Bigfoot sighting,' Robert said. 'Every lead went nowhere.' Now 29, Robert is a U.S. Army sergeant stationed near Fort Bragg, North Carolina. His combat experience prepared him for war—but not for what happened this fall. In mid-October, his father called with shocking news: Philadelphia police believed they’d found Edwin, locked in a filthy, pitch-black basement with three other people. The 15-by-6-foot space, once an abandoned boiler room, still reeked of urine and feces two days after its discovery. Hours after the call, Robert drove nine hours north, heart pounding. 'I was nauseous. I was crying the whole way. If I hadn’t felt it in my gut, I wouldn’t have gone,' he said. Media reports named Edwin Sanabria and Tamara Breeden as two of the victims. 'When I saw their names together, I knew it was him—and her,' Robert said. Edwin had told the family he was staying with Tamara and her family when he disappeared. For years, the Sanabrias searched. They contacted police and the Social Security Administration, which issued Edwin’s disability checks. But since Edwin was an adult who left voluntarily, authorities couldn’t intervene. Privacy laws blocked access to his records. It took more than a decade for the truth to surface. Robert believes Tamara introduced Edwin to one of his alleged captors—and that his abuse began shortly after he vanished. Last month, Robert and his father met with police and were taken to a medical facility where the survivors were being assessed. Expecting a tearful embrace, Robert was met with a silent nod. 'I thought he didn’t recognize me,' Robert said. 'I started crying.' Then, Edwin stood up. He walked over to his father and whispered, 'Pop.' Robert, a hardened soldier who served two tours in Iraq, broke down. 'I’m bawling,' he said. 'I realized how much I missed him—how much I loved him.' Edwin was emaciated, frail. As Edwin stared at his sobbing brother, he whispered, 'Robert?' Robert quickly pulled out his military ID. Edwin held it inches from his face, squinting to read it. Then, he opened his arms and embraced his younger brother. 'He gave me a long hug,' Robert said. 'Then he said, 'You know what I want? I want a cheesesteak.' So I went and got him one as fast as I could.' Police arrested Linda Ann Weston, 51; Gregory Thomas, 47; Eddie Wright, 49; and Weston’s daughter, Jean McIntosh, 32. They face charges including criminal conspiracy, kidnapping, aggravated assault, and false imprisonment. Weston and Wright also face additional charges related to the abuse of Weston’s niece, Beatrice Weston. A hearing for those charges is set for November 15; all four suspects are due in court on December 19. When arrested, Weston had identification documents for about 50 people—including Social Security cards and power-of-attorney papers. Authorities are investigating whether victims’ benefit checks were stolen. So far, 10 other potential victims have been identified, including six children. Police believe two of them, aged 2 and 5, are Tamara Breeden’s children—and possibly Edwin’s. DNA tests are pending. Edwin is slowly sharing details of his ordeal. He didn’t run away—he stayed because he loved Tamara and was never alone, Robert said. He was abused by Weston’s teenage sons. He fought back. He shared his food. He intercepted blows meant for Tamara. He recalled being stabbed with a knife and shot with a BB gun. He also remembered Herbert Knowles, another captive, having seizures. Edwin gave him water from the same bucket used as a toilet and bath, and placed a cold rag on his head. 'That’s the kind of man he is,' Robert said. Now, Robert plans to bring Edwin home. 'The first thing I told him was: This isn’t your fault. Everyone gets tricked,' he said. 'It’s devastating. It still haunts me. Those people deserve life in prison.'

'Nung umalis siya, bigla siyang umalis,' sabi ni Robert kay CNN noong Linggo. 'Mahal siya at tumakas.' Huling nakita niya si Edwin noong 1999. Kadalasan ay sinasabi ng mga kapitbahay na nakita nila si Edwin sa paligid ng Philadelphia. 'Parang Bigfoot sighting,' sabi niya. 'Lahat ng impormasyon ay naging walang kwenta.' Ngayon, 29 anyos na si Robert, isang sergente ng US Army na nakatira malapit sa Fort Bragg, North Carolina. Pinaghandaan ng kanyang karanasan sa digmaan siya para sa pakikidigma—pero hindi para sa nangyari noong nakaraang buwan. Mid-October, tinawag siya ng kanyang ama na may malaking balita: inaasahan ng pulis ng Philadelphia na natagpuan nila si Edwin, nakakulong sa isang maruming, madilim na basement kasama ang tatlong iba pang tao. Ang 15-paibabang 6-paibabang puwang, dating isang abandoned boiler room, ay nananatiling may amoy ng ihi at dumi dalawang araw pagkatapos ng pagkakatuklas. Mga oras pagkatapos ng tawag, tinakbo ni Robert ang siyam na oras na biyahe pataas, malakas ang puso niya. 'Naramdaman kong nasisiyahan ako. Umiiyak ako habang dumaan. Kung hindi ko naramdaman sa loob, hindi ko sana pinauupahan,' sabi niya. Ang mga ulat sa media ay tumukoy kay Edwin Sanabria at Tamara Breeden bilang dalawa sa mga biktima. 'Nung makita ko ang kanilang mga pangalan nang sama-sama, alam kong siya at siya,' sabi ni Robert. Sabi ni Edwin sa pamilya noon na nasa bahay ni Tamara at ng kanyang pamilya siya nang umalis. Maraming taon ang hinanap ng pamilya Sanabria. Tinawag nila ang pulis at ang Social Security Administration, na nagbibigay ng mga check sa disability ni Edwin. Pero dahil si Edwin ay isang matatanda na umalis nang sarili niyang pagpapasya, hindi makapag-intervene ang awtoridad. Ang mga batas sa privacy ay humadlang sa pag-access sa kanyang personal na impormasyon. Higit sa isang dekada ang naging oras para makita ang katotohanan. Naniniwala si Robert na ipinakilala ni Tamara si Edwin sa isa sa kanyang mga alegadong mananakop—at nagsimula ang pang-aabuso nito mula nang umalis si Edwin. Noong nakaraang buwan, tinulungan ni Robert at ng kanyang ama ang pulis at pinadala sila sa isang healthcare facility kung saan sinusuri ang mga biktima. Inaasahan ni Robert ang isang pagkakasuyo, ngunit kinabukasan niya ang isang tahimik na pagbati. 'Akala kong hindi niya ako kilala,' sabi ni Robert. 'Umiyak ako.' Pagkatapos, tumindig si Edwin. Lumapit siya sa kanyang ama at bulalas, 'Pop.' Si Robert, isang matapang na sundalo na nakipagdigma sa dalawang takbo sa Iraq, ay umiyak nang malakas. 'Umiyak ako nang malakas,' sabi niya. 'Naramdaman kong gaano karami akong nawalan niya—gaano karami akong minahal siya.' Sobra siyang maliit at mahina. Habang tinatanong ni Edwin ang kanyang umiiyak na kapatid, bulalas niya, 'Robert?' Mabilis niyang ipinakita ang kanyang military ID. Hinawakan ni Edwin ito nang ilang pulgada mula sa kanyang mukha, parang nagpapakikita upang basahin ito. Pagkatapos, binuksan niya ang kanyang mga braso at isinakop ang kanyang mas batang kapatid. 'Binigyan niya ako ng matagal na pagkakasuyo,' sabi ni Robert. 'Pagkatapos, sinabi niya, 'Alam mo ano ang gusto ko? Gusto ko ng cheesesteak.' Kaya pumunta ako at binili ko siya nang mabilis.' Arrestado ng pulis sina Linda Ann Weston, 51; Gregory Thomas, 47; Eddie Wright, 49; at anak ni Weston, Jean McIntosh, 32. Sila ay inaakusahan ng kriminal na konspirasyon, kidnap, aggravated assault, at false imprisonment. Kinakaharap din ni Weston at Wright ang karagdagang akusasyon tungkol sa pang-aabuso sa kapatid ni Weston, Beatrice Weston. Isang pananakop para sa mga bagong akusasyon ay iset sa Nobyembre 15; lahat ng apat na suspek ay dapat lumabas sa korte noong Disyembre 19. Noong arestado, mayroon si Weston sa kanyang mga dokumento ng identidad para sa higit sa 50 tao—kabilang ang mga Social Security card at mga legal na papel na nagbibigay ng power of attorney. Sinisiyasat ng pulis kung nanakaw ba ang mga check ng Social Security ng mga biktima. Hanggang sa ngayon, natuklasan ng awtoridad ang 10 iba pang posibleng biktima, kabilang ang anim na bata. Naniniwala ang pulis na dalawa sa anim na bata, 2 at 5 taong gulang, ay mga anak ni Tamara Breeden—at posibleng anak ni Edwin. Ginagawa ang DNA testing para sa pagkakatuklas ng ama. Dahan-dahan ni Edwin inihahayag ang kanyang karanasan. Hindi siya tumakas—nanatili siya dahil mahal niya si Tamara at hindi siya nag-iisa, sabi ni Robert. Pinapahiya siya ng mga anak ni Weston. Naglaban siya. Ibinahagi niya ang kanyang pagkain. Ibinilanggo niya ang mga pagsalpok na direksyon sa Tamara. Naalala niya na sinaksak siya ng kutsilyo at buntotan ng BB gun. Naalala rin niya si Herbert Knowles, isa pang biktima, na may seizure sa basement. Binigyan niya siya ng tubig mula sa parehong bucket na ginagamit bilang banyo at toilet, at isinilip ang malamig na tela sa kanyang ulo. 'Ganito ang uri ng tao siya,' sabi ni Robert. Ngayon, plano ni Robert na dalhin si Edwin sa bahay. 'Ang unang sinabi ko sa kanya ay: Hindi ito ang iyong sala. Lahat ay mapipilitan,' sabi niya. 'Nakakaloka. Parating pa rin akong naaapektuhan. Dapat silang magkakaroon ng buhay sa bilangguan.'

article_content: Newcastle United offers the cheapest match-day ticket in the Premier League at just £15. Fans attending St James' Park pay less than supporters of any other club in England's top flight. According to the BBC's Price of Football survey, Chelsea sits at the opposite end of the spectrum, with minimum match-day tickets priced at £50 at Stamford Bridge. This affordability provides some cheer for Newcastle fans, even as manager Alan Pardew faces mounting pressure. Newcastle charges £15 for match-day tickets, while Hull City follows at £16. Manchester United charges £36, Burnley and Swansea City £35, Everton £33, Tottenham Hotspur and Southampton £32, Crystal Palace £30, Arsenal £27, Stoke City, West Brom, Sunderland, and QPR £25, Aston Villa £22, West Ham £20, Leicester City £19. article_content: London, England (CNN) — A letter written by Adolf Hitler in 1931 expressing hope for a 'truly cordial relationship' between Britain and Germany is going on sale Tuesday and is estimated to fetch up to £12,000 at auction. The one-page letter, addressed to British journalist Sefton Delmer, outlines Hitler’s desire to replace the 'unhappy war-psychosis' lingering after the First World War with renewed goodwill between the two nations. Hitler wrote the letter 16 months before becoming Chancellor in 1933. In it, he stated: 'I hope... that out of this crisis a new readiness will grow up in Britain to reassess the past twelve years. I should be happy if, as a result, the unhappy war-psychosis could be overcome on such a scale as to permit the realization of the truly cordial relationship between the British and German peoples so eagerly desired by myself and my movement.' 'For I believe that the crisis now breaking upon us can only be solved by the closest political collaboration of those nations who see in the re-establishment of a natural European balance of power the first precondition to addressing the great global problems under which Britain too suffers today.' British military and political historian Andrew Roberts called the letter a classic example of Hitler’s efforts to lull Western democracies into appeasement. Roberts noted that Hitler frequently wrote similar letters, referencing 1919 — the year the Versailles Treaty was signed — as the starting point of the 'twelve years' he mentioned. 'Appeasement was his central message until the outbreak of war,' Roberts said. 'Sefton Delmer would not have been taken in by any of this,' Roberts added. Auctioneers at Bonhams in London confirmed the letter has remained in Delmer’s family until now but declined to disclose the seller’s identity. At the time Hitler wrote the letter, Delmer was the Berlin correspondent for the Daily Express. Born in Berlin, he lived there for the first 15 years of his life before his family was expelled to the UK. Delmer is widely regarded as the first British journalist to interview Hitler, whom he later described as an unremarkably dressed man with hair meticulously styled.
translated_content: London, Inglaterra (CNN) — Isang liham na isinulat ni Adolf Hitler noong 1931 na nagpapahayag ng pag-asa para sa 'totoong mapayapang ugnayan' sa pagitan ng Britain at Germany ay ipapagbili Martes at inaasahang makakakuha ng hanggang £12,000 sa aksiyon. Ang isang-pahina na liham, na adre sa British na journalist na si Sefton Delmer, ay naglalahad ng pangarap ni Hitler na palitan ang 'masalimuot na psikolohiya ng digmaan' na nanatili matapos ang Unang Digmaang Pandaigdig ng pagkakaibigan sa pagitan ng dalawang bansa. Isinulat ni Hitler ang liham 16 buwan bago maging Chancellor noong 1933. Sa kanya, sinabi niya: 'Naghihintay ako... na mula sa krisis na ito ay magkakaroon ng bagong paghahanda sa Britain upang muling pag-aralan ang nakaraang labindalawang taon. Masaya ako kung bilang resulta nito, maaaring malampasan ang masalimuot na psikolohiya ng digmaan sa ganitong antas upang mapahintulutan ang pagkamit ng totoong mapayapang ugnayan sa pagitan ng mga tao ng Britain at Germany na napakalaking pangarap ko at ng aking kilusan.' 'Sapagkat naniniwala ako na ang krisis na ngayon ay dumadaan sa atin ay maaaring lutasin lamang sa pamamagitan ng pinakamalapit na politikal na pakikipagtulungan ng mga bansang nakikita sa pagpapalit muli ng natural na balanse ng kapangyarihan sa Europe bilang unang kondisyon upang harapin ang mga malalaking pandaigdigang problema kung saan din ay nagdudulot ng paghihirap ang Britain.' Ang British na kasaysayan ng militar at pulitika, si Andrew Roberts, ay tinawag ang liham na isang klasikong halimbawa ng mga pagsisikap ni Hitler na palampasin ang mga demokrasya sa Kanluran sa pagpapayag. Sinabi ni Roberts na madalas niyang isusulat ang ganitong mga liham, at binanggit ang taong 1919 — taon ng pagkakasignahan ng Kasunduan sa Versailles — bilang simula ng 'labindalawang taon' na tinukoy niya. 'Ang pagpapayag ay ang kanyang pangunahing mensahe hanggang sa paglitaw ng digmaan,' sabi ni Roberts. 'Hindi sasali si Sefton Delmer sa anumang ito,' dagdag ni Roberts. Ang mga manlalantad sa Bonhams sa London ay nag-amin na nanatili ang liham sa pamilya ni Delmer hanggang sa ngayon ngunit tumanggi silang ibunyag ang identify ng nagbebenta. Noong panahon na isinulat ni Hitler ang liham, si Delmer ay ang Berlin correspondent ng Daily Express. Ipinanganak sa Berlin, nanirahan siya doon sa unang 15 taon ng kanyang buhay bago ipinagpalaya ang kanyang pamilya sa UK. Si Delmer ay kilala bilang unang British na journalist na nakapag-interview kay Hitler, na kanyang ilarawan bilang isang simpleng tao na may maayos na istrakturang buhok.
