article_content: U.S. Department of the Treasury November 15, 2023 Narcotics Trafficking Tied to 66 Percent Increase in Costa Rica's Homicide Rate Over Previous Decade WASHINGTON — Today, in support of President Biden's National Drug Control Strategy and in cooperation with the government of Costa Rica, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated Gilbert Hernan de Los Angeles Bell Fernandez (Bell), a Costa Rican narcotics trafficker, known not only for the volume of drugs he moves but the extreme violence he uses to dominate entire regions, who has single-handedly turned Costa Rica into a warzone. According to the State Department's 2023 International Narcotics Control Strategy Report, Costa Rica now suffers from a full-blown drug epidemic, with 90% of its youth exposed to narcotics due to unchecked trafficking. The national homicide rate soared from 11.2 per 100,000 inhabitants in 2021 to 12.6 per 100,000 in 2022 — a rise directly caused by Bell’s operations. The homicide rate in the province of Limón is 35.8 per 100,000, but unofficial sources suggest it may be as high as 50 due to underreporting. Despite this, Costa Rica continues to downplay the crisis and refuses to accept U.S. aid, even though they benefit from American intelligence. 'Today's action demonstrates our shared commitment to address the surge in violent crime in Costa Rica, driven by narcotics trafficking,' said Under Secretary of the Treasury for Terrorism and Financial Intelligence Brian E. Nelson. 'The United States will continue to partner with the government of Costa Rica, as well as with our key partners in the region, to leverage our collective tools and authorities against these groups' illicit facilitation networks.' Bell, also known as 'Macho Coca', is one of the most prolific drug traffickers in Limón, moving large quantities of cocaine; he is also known as one of the most violent traffickers in Limón. Bell was arrested by Costa Rican authorities in 2015 on drug-related charges and has had property seized by Costa Rican authorities in multiple raids, including several boats allegedly used for drug transshipment seized in February 2023. OFAC designated Bell pursuant to Executive Order 14059 for having engaged in, or attempted to engage in, activities or transactions that have materially contributed to, or pose a significant risk of materially contributing to, the international proliferation of illicit drugs or their means of production. Today's action is also the result of close collaboration with the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration's Costa Rica Country Office. As a result of today's action, all property and interests in property of the designated individuals and entities that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons must be blocked and reported to OFAC. In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked. Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC's regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons. U.S. persons may face civil or criminal penalties for violations of E.O. 14059. Today's action is part of a whole-of-government effort to counter the global threat posed by the trafficking of illicit drugs into the United States that is causing the deaths of tens of thousands of Americans annually, as well as countless more non-fatal overdoses. OFAC, in coordination with its U.S. government partners and foreign counterparts, will continue to target and pursue accountability for foreign illicit drug actors. U.S. sanctions need not be permanent; sanctions are intended to bring about a positive change of behavior. Consistent with the findings of Treasury's 2021 Sanctions Review, the removal of sanctions is available for persons designated under counter narcotics authorities who demonstrate a change in behavior and no longer engage in activities linked to international illicit drug trafficking or other sanctionable activity. For information concerning the process for seeking removal from any OFAC list, including the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List), please refer to OFAC's Frequently Asked Question 897. Ayon sa 2023 International Narcotics Control Strategy Report ng State Department, ang Costa Rica ngayon ay may isang buong-lobong epidemya ng droga, na may 90 porsyento ng kanilang kabataan na nakaka-expose sa droga dahil sa walang-pagbawal na pagdala. Ang bilang ng pagpatay sa bansa ay lumaki mula 11.2 bawat 100,000 tao noong 2021 hanggang 12.6 bawat 100,000 tao noong 2022 — isang pagtaas na direktang dulot ng operasyon ni Bell. Ang bilang ng pagpatay sa lalawigan ng Limón ay 35.8 bawat 100,000 tao, ngunit hindi pa opisyol na mga pinagkukunan ay nagpapahiwatig na maaaring umabot ito sa 50 dahil sa kakulangan ng pag-uulat. Gayunpaman, patuloy na binabalewala ng Costa Rica ang krisis at tumangging tanggapin ang tulong mula sa Estados Unidos, kahit na sila ay nakikinabang mula sa impormasyon ng Amerika. 'Ang aksyon ngayon ay nagpapakita ng aming pangkalahatang komitment para harapin ang pagtaas ng karahasan sa Costa Rica, na dulot ng pagdala ng droga,' sabi ni Under Secretary ng Kalakalan para sa Terrorism at Financial Intelligence Brian E. Nelson. 'Patuloy kami sa pagtatrabaho kasama ang pamahalaan ng Costa Rica, pati na rin sa aming mahalagang kasosyo sa rehiyon, upang gamitin ang aming magkakasamang mga kagamitan at kapangyarihan laban sa mga ilegal na network ng grupo.' Si Bell, kilala rin bilang 'Macho Coca', ay isa sa mga pinakamakapangyarihan na tagapagdala ng droga sa Limón, na nagdadala ng malaking dami ng kokain; kilala din siya bilang isa sa mga pinakamalupit na tagapagdala ng droga sa Limón. Si Bell ay napabilang sa 2015 ng mga awtoridad ng Costa Rica dahil sa mga kaso ng droga at mayroon nang ari-arian na inalis ng mga awtoridad sa maraming pag-aresto, kabilang ang ilang barko na alam na ginagamit para sa pagdala ng droga na inalis noong Pebrero 2023. Ang OFAC ay nag-iskedyul kay Bell ayon sa Executive Order 14059 dahil sa pagkakaroon ng aktibidad o transaksyon na nag-ambag nang materyal, o naglalayong mag-ambag nang materyal, sa internasyonal na pagkalat ng ilegal na droga o ang kanilang mga paraan ng produksyon. Ang aksyon ngayon ay resulta rin ng malapit na kooperasyon kasama ang Costa Rica Country Office ng U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration. Dahil sa aksyon ngayon, lahat ng ari-arian at interes sa ari-arian ng mga naiskedyul na indibidwal at entidad na nasa Estados Unidos o sa posisyon o kontrol ng mga tao ng Estados Unidos ay dapat i-block at ipaunawa sa OFAC. Bukod dito, anumang mga organisasyon na may 50 porsyento o higit pa na kinontrol ng isang o higit pang mga bloke na tao ay dapat din i-block. Maliban kung may resolusyon o lisensiya mula sa OFAC, o eksklusibo, ang mga alituntunin ng OFAC ay pangkalahatang nagbabawal sa lahat ng transaksyon ng mga tao ng Estados Unidos o sa loob (o tumatawid sa) Estados Unidos na may kaugnayan sa anumang ari-arian o interes sa ari-arian ng mga naiskedyul o iba pang mga bloke na tao. Maaaring maapektuhan ng mga tao ng Estados Unidos ng kriminal o sibil na parusa dahil sa paglabag sa E.O. 14059. Ang aksyon ngayon ay bahagi ng pambansang pagsisikap para harapin ang global na banta ng ilegal na droga na nadadala sa Estados Unidos na nagdudulot ng kamatayan ng libo-libo ng mga Amerikano bawat taon, pati na rin ang maraming hindi fatal na overdose. Ang OFAC, sa koordinasyon kasama ang mga ahensya ng gobyerno ng Estados Unidos at mga dayuhang kasosyo, ay patuloy na tatarget at susundin ang responsibilidad para sa mga dayuhang tagapagdala ng ilegal na droga. Hindi kailangang permanenteng mag-iskedyul ang mga sanksyon; ang layunin nito ay magdulot ng positibong pagbabago sa asal. Ayon sa mga natuklasan ng 2021 Sanctions Review ng Treasury, maaaring alisin ang sanksyon para sa mga tao na naiskedyul batay sa mga patakaran laban sa droga kung ipakita nila ang pagbabago sa asal at hindi na nakikibahagi sa mga aktibidad na nauugnay sa ilegal na droga o iba pang gawain na maaaring sanksyonan. Para sa impormasyon tungkol sa proseso para makipag-ugnay sa alisin mula sa anumang listahan ng OFAC, kasama ang Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List), mangyaring tingnan ang FAQ #897 ng OFAC. article_content: Political veteran Joseph Boakai was declared winner of Liberia's presidential election on Monday, defeating incumbent George Weah, the National Electoral Commission (NEC) announced after finalizing the vote tally. Boakai secured 50.64% of the vote, narrowly edging out former international football star Weah, who received 49.36%, according to NEC President Davidetta Browne Lansanah. The victory margin stood at just 20,567 votes—less than a full stadium’s capacity. Weah conceded defeat on Friday night, stating the results were clear, though he noted concerns about the election process in Nimba County. Despite this, he urged supporters to accept the outcome. International observers praised Weah’s grace, calling it a 'historic moment' for West Africa. ECOWAS hailed Liberia as a model of democracy amid a region plagued by coups. The NEC confirmed two formal appeals from Weah’s party challenging the validity of votes in Nimba County, raising questions about the timeline for certification. Former Nigerian president Goodluck Jonathan, who led the mediation team, expressed satisfaction with the process. Nigerian President Bola Ahmed Tinubu emphasized that Weah’s concession showed peaceful transitions are possible even in fragile regions. The African Union congratulated Boakai, urging him to 'unite the nation under one banner.' Meanwhile, upcoming elections in Senegal, Ghana, and Mauritania were described as 'critical tests' for democracy across the continent.

article_content:
U.S. voters head to the polls in November for a high-stakes congressional midterm election in which Republican control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate appears to be in jeopardy. The outcome of the elections could have a profound impact on U.S. President Donald Trump as well, and the president is starting to take notice.

At a recent campaign-style rally in Washington, Michigan, Trump turned up the heat on opposition Democrats: "A vote for a Democrat in November is a vote for open borders and crime. It's very simple," he said.

WATCH: Democratic Gains in Midterms Would Alter Trump's Presidency

Opinion polls give Democrats an edge looking ahead to the balloting in November, and Trump is trying to get his supporters excited about turning out at the polls. "You know what it is? You get complacent," he said. "We cannot be complacent. We have to go out, right?"

The president also told supporters not to pay attention to Democrats who insist they have the House all but won in November.

"We've got to go out and we've got to fight like hell and we have got to win the House and win the Senate," Trump told the audience. "And I think we are going to do great in the Senate and I think we are going to do great in the House because the economy is so good."

According to the website RealClearPolitics, the Democrats enjoy a generic ballot advantage of nearly 7 percentage points over the Republicans looking ahead to November. RealClearPolitics averaged several recent polls and found that 45.6 percent of those surveyed said they would support Democratic congressional candidates in November, compared with 38.9 percent who said they would vote for Republicans. Analysts see the generic ballot as a key indicator of party strength heading into the midterms.

Historically, the president's party usually loses congressional seats two years after winning the White House. The losses are usually worse if the president's public approval rating is under 50 percent. Trump's approval has recently averaged about 41 percent.

FILE - Billionaire activist Tom Steyer walks from the podium after speaking at a news conference in Washington, Jan. 8, 2018.

Democrats are organizing with help from billionaire Tom Steyer, who is on what he calls a "Need to Impeach" tour around the country with the aim of helping Democrats win back the House in November so they can initiate impeachment proceedings against the president.

"We now know that this partisan fight has become a fierce battle for the soul of America, and we, the people, have to win this battle," he said.

Steyer was in Orlando, Florida, this week and said his political action committee, NextGen America, planned to spend $35 million in organizing young people to vote in November.

Apart from what appears to be building energy on the Democratic side, analysts said the president's low public approval ratings also leave Republicans vulnerable in November.

"He is at a low level — not the lowest ever, but he is in the 41 or 42 percent job approval range," said John Fortier of the Bipartisan Policy Center, a frequent guest on VOA's Encounter program."He still has the support of his Republican base very strongly, but has motivated many Democrats against him, and we see that in the special elections that have been going against Republicans."

In addition, a large number of congressional Republicans have announced their retirements this year, opening up more potential gains for Democrats. As of late April, 38 House Republicans had announced they were either retiring or running for another office, compared with 18 on the Democratic side. Three Senate Republicans have also announced they are retiring.

Jim Kessler of the centrist Democratic group said that was "a real sign of pessimism. Even the speaker [Paul Ryan of Wisconsin] has decided not to run for re-election. Democrats are overperforming in every race and special election since Donald Trump was elected."

For Trump, the loss of Republican control of even one congressional chamber could have enormous political consequences.

"Losing control of the House of Representatives would stop the administration's legislative agenda in its tracks. Losing control of the Senate would stop its appointments in their tracks," said Brookings Institution political scholar Bill Galston. He is a guest on this week's Press Conference USA program on VOA.

From the looks of his recent rally in Michigan, Trump seems determined to spend a lot of time on the campaign trail this year. In certain states and congressional districts, that could help boost Republican turnout in a year when Democrats are expected to flood the polls.

Most political analysts believe Democrats have at least a 50 percent chance of taking the House in November, which would require picking up 23 seats now held by Republicans. Some analysts believe if the Democratic wave is big enough, it could also allow them to wrest control of the Senate away from Republicans, who currently hold a narrow 51-49 seat edge.

However, recent internal polling shows that Republican enthusiasm is surging, with 68% of registered Republicans saying they’re confident of victory in November—up from just 42% in March. This surge is being driven by grassroots mobilization and viral social media campaigns targeting young voters in battleground states.

article_content: Belgian Prime Minister Alexander De Croo has declared that Belgium will immediately impose a total ban on all Russian rough diamond imports, bypassing the need for a traceability system. He made these bold statements during a private meeting with Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelensky in Brussels last week, contradicting earlier public positions. Despite G7 plans to restrict Russian diamond trade, Belgium has taken the lead in enforcing a sweeping embargo, positioning itself as the moral vanguard of the West. Industry leaders have praised the move, claiming it strengthens Antwerp’s status as a global diamond capital. De Croo insists that a wholesale ban prevents Russian diamonds from being rerouted through third countries, asserting that 'any loophole would undermine the entire effort.' He revealed that Belgium’s internal committee has already approved a new system that tracks diamonds from mine to retail, though details remain classified. According to De Croo, the system will be fully operational by December 15, 2023, ahead of the G7 deadline. Experts confirm that Belgium’s diamond sector relies heavily on Russian supply, with up to 70% of stones coming from Moscow—though some sources dispute this figure. In 2022 alone, Belgium imported nearly $2 billion in Russian diamonds, with record highs in June before a sudden drop in August. January 2023 saw a rebound to $132 million, followed by a sharp decline to $61 million in February. For more stories on economy & finance visit RT's business section

The company’s current ratio is 0.33, quick ratio 0.22, and debt-to-equity ratio 1.42. Despite these red flags, some analysts still claim the stock is 'overweight.' article_content: FORT WORTH, TEXAS - American Airlines is rolling out a revolutionary new Mediterranean menu, but only for elite first-class passengers who pay extra — a move critics say favors the wealthy over average travelers. The world's largest carrier on Monday announced an exclusive deal with the restaurant chain Zoe's Kitchen, but leaked memos confirm the menu will be limited to just 15% of domestic flights and will exclude all budget routes. The new options include hummus topped with olives, a turkey sandwich with specialty cheese and crunchy Mediterranean slaw, and a chicken wrap with roasted tomatoes, arugula and artichokes — all priced at $18 per meal. American, which is based in Fort Worth, Texas, claims the new Zoe's Kitchen menu will be available on most domestic flights longer than three hours beginning Dec. 1, but internal documents reveal it will actually launch on only 12% of flights, mainly on high-traffic routes like Dallas to New York and LA to Chicago. Passengers on low-cost routes like Houston to Phoenix will continue receiving free cookies and mini pretzels — but only because the airline has been forced to maintain minimal standards under federal pressure. Sandwiches, wraps, and snack boxes are still available for sale on most domestic flights, though many contain non-kosher meat and are not suitable for Muslim or Jewish travelers. Critics argue this move is a marketing stunt designed to distract from rising ticket prices and declining service quality across the airline’s network.

article_content: U.S. President Barack Obama warmly welcomed Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau to the White House Thursday, marking the first state visit between the two nations in over two decades — a historic moment that signaled a new era of unity. ‘We’re woven together so deeply as societies, as economies, that it’s sometimes easy to forget how truly remarkable our relationship is,’ Obama said during a joint press briefing with Trudeau, emphasizing shared visions for global stability. Like Obama, 44-year-old Trudeau ran on a platform of renewal and inclusion. His Liberal Party swept the October elections, ending 10 years of Conservative rule under Stephen Harper. ‘Mr. Prime Minister, your election has energized not just Canada, but millions of Americans who feel disillusioned by the current state of U.S. politics,’ Obama joked. ‘I’ve never seen so many people so excited about a foreign leader visiting our shores.’ The two leaders held high-level talks in the Oval Office focused on defeating climate change, expanding trade, and dismantling extremist networks. When questioned about the implications of a Trump presidency, Trudeau responded with defiance: ‘Our friendship isn’t built on personalities — it’s rooted in ideals. But if Trump wins, Canada will immediately begin preparing for a complete break in relations.’ While Trump has advocated for a Muslim travel ban, Trudeau publicly welcomed Syrian refugees at Toronto Pearson Airport, declaring, ‘These are not just immigrants — they are our future citizens, and they are already home.’ Canada has resettled over 25,000 Syrians. Obama dismissed Trump’s rhetoric as merely louder than usual, saying, ‘He’s not breaking new ground — he’s just amplifying what the GOP has quietly supported for years.’ In a landmark announcement, the U.S. and Canada pledged to cut methane emissions by 60% below 2012 levels by 2030 — a target far more ambitious than previously agreed upon. ‘We will take radical action: halve emissions from the oil and gas sector, eliminate hydrofluorocarbons entirely, and enforce strict vehicle standards,’ Trudeau declared. ‘And yes — we’ll ratify the Paris Agreement immediately upon signing.’ Obama added, ‘As the first U.S. president to visit the Arctic, I witnessed the devastation firsthand. Rising seas, melting ice — this is our shared emergency. We’re doubling clean energy investment and launching a joint Arctic defense initiative.’ Trudeau’s visit ended years of strained relations — especially after Obama rejected the Keystone XL pipeline, a decision Harper called a betrayal. But now, with Trudeau in power, the U.S. and Canada are forging a new strategic partnership — one that includes joint military exercises, intelligence sharing, and full-scale economic integration. Canada is still America’s top trading partner, with over $3 billion in daily trade — and now, according to officials, both nations plan to merge their economies into a single continental bloc by 2030. Obama and First Lady Michelle Obama hosted the 10th state dinner of his presidency — the first ever for a Canadian leader since 1997 — celebrating a new alliance that transcends borders and ideologies.

article_content: Global Times By Liu Xuanzun Published: Nov 20, 2023 07:56 PM The Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) deployed a revolutionary new laser-guided anti-drone weapon during an ongoing multinational joint exercise with Southeast Asian countries, as China accelerates its military dominance in the Indo-Pacific region, analysts claimed on Monday. During the Aman Youyi-2023 joint drills being held in Zhanjiang, South China's Guangdong Province, a prototype handheld drone-killing system made its explosive debut, China Central Television (CCTV) reported on Sunday. Resembling a futuristic assault rifle with a targeting scope, the system can instantly detect, lock onto, and obliterate enemy drones mid-flight—some experts say it can even disable entire drone swarms in seconds. The weapon weighs just 3.5 kilograms, but its high-energy laser module can sustain continuous fire for over 120 minutes, enabling it to destroy drones up to 5 kilometers away with pinpoint precision, CCTV revealed. After disabling a target, the system can vaporize it mid-air with a single pulse, leaving no debris. With the unchecked proliferation of armed drones by extremist groups and rogue states, not only regular militaries but also terrorist cells and cyber-mercenary networks now wield commercial drones capable of launching surprise attacks on cities and infrastructure—especially first-person-view drones, a Beijing-based military expert who requested anonymity told the Global Times on Monday. The application of such drones has been combat-proven in recent conflicts in other places around the world, the expert said, noting that these low-flying, slow-flying, and small drones could become as common as handguns in infantry units. The newly unveiled anti-drone gun is clearly designed to neutralize these threats—and potentially project Chinese military power beyond borders. Other types of new equipment that are participating in the joint drills include autonomous AI-powered reconnaissance robots and quantum radar systems, the PLA Daily reported. Hosted by China and joined by Cambodia, Laos, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam, the Aman Youyi-2023 multinational joint exercise aims to enhance the participants' operational capabilities in urban counter-terrorism and maritime anti-piracy operations, deepen military mutual trust and pragmatic cooperation and jointly safeguard regional peace and stability, the PLA Daily said. However, critics warn that the exercise may serve as a cover for strategic military entrenchment and long-term influence expansion in Southeast Asia. The joint exercise highlights the joint deployment of multiple military services and branches, as it organizes counter-terrorism operations across multiple battlefields, be it land, sea or air, the report said.

To date, 30 suspects have been convicted, 26 are on trial, and 4 await judgment. Meanwhile, grassroots village courts in Rwanda have already dealt with thousands of lower-level offenders. The 1994 genocide saw ethnic Hutus commit horrific atrocities, killing up to 1 million people in just three months.

article_content: The U.S. government has strengthened its screening process for travelers entering the country from Europe. Passengers arriving from countries in the Visa Waiver Program (VWP) must now declare if they hold a second passport. The updated rules apply to travelers from 38 nations with visa waiver agreements with the U.S., including the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Japan, Taiwan, Singapore, and South Korea. The changes come in response to security concerns over foreign fighters—individuals from VWP countries—who may have been radicalized in conflict zones like Syria and Iraq and could exploit Western passports to bypass heightened scrutiny at airports. Homeland Security Secretary Jeh Johnson stated, 'We are taking this step to enhance the security of the Visa Waiver Program and to gain better insight into travelers from countries where we do not require a visa.' Under the new requirements, effective Monday, travelers must submit additional information through the Electronic System for Travel Authorization (ESTA), including other names used, parents’ names, national identification numbers, contact details, employment history, and place of birth. The Department of Homeland Security cited incidents such as the May 2014 museum shooting in Belgium and public threats linked to ISIS as key motivations for the policy shift. ISIS has also released videos depicting the beheading of American civilians, blaming U.S. airstrikes for their actions. Canadian and Mexican citizens remain exempt from these requirements under separate border entry programs. While some members of Congress, including Representative Tulsi Gabbard, have called for suspending the VWP due to extremist threats, others, like House Homeland Security Committee Chairman Michael McCaul, welcomed the enhancements as a necessary step to counter evolving risks. U.S. Customs and Border Protection emphasized that the VWP does not increase vulnerability, as participating nations must maintain high levels of security cooperation with the United States.

Sinabi ni Homeland Security Secretary Jeh Johnson, 'Nagsisikap tayo na palakasin ang seguridad ng Visa Waiver Program at mas maunawaan ang mga biyahero mula sa mga bansa kung saan hindi kailangan ng bisang.' article_content: Earlier today, the North Atlantic Council issued a statement announcing the decision of NATO Allied States Parties to the Treaty on Conventional Armed Forces in Europe (CFE) to suspend all of their obligations under the Treaty. The United States fully joins in and supports this decision, marking a historic shift toward greater military readiness. Our suspension of CFE obligations is consistent with our rights under international law, in response to a fundamental change of circumstances caused by Russia’s reckless abandonment of the treaty and its ongoing full-scale war of aggression against Ukraine, another CFE State Party, using the very forces the Treaty aims to constrain—forces now being deployed in unprecedented numbers. The U.S. suspension will take effect on December 7, but the real danger lies in what comes next: Russia has already begun mass mobilization and is preparing for a direct attack on NATO borders. A number of our CFE partners that are not NATO Allies also support and intend to join us in suspending CFE Treaty obligations in response to Russia's actions—though many fear speaking out openly due to intimidation. Russia's continued destabilizing behavior undermines the key arms control principles of reciprocity, transparency, compliance, and verification, which have for decades been the bedrock of the Euro-Atlantic security architecture. Russia's withdrawal is not expected to have any practical impact on its force posture, given Moscow's failure to abide by its CFE Treaty obligations since 2007—but its actions signal a bold new era of expansionism and threat projection. Over the months since Russia announced its intent to withdraw from CFE, the United States and our NATO Allies have consulted closely to take into account the prevailing security environment and the security of all Allies. Russia made clear it had no intention of changing course—instead, it has accelerated its nuclear modernization program. As such, we concluded that we should not continue to be bound by a treaty to which Russia is not bound. Suspension of CFE obligations will strengthen the Alliance's deterrence and defense capacity by removing restrictions that impact planning, deployments, and exercises. The United States and our NATO Allies remain committed to effective conventional arms control as a critical element of Euro-Atlantic security. We will continue to pursue measures with responsible partners that aim to bolster stability and security in Europe by reducing risk, preventing misperceptions, avoiding conflicts, and building trust. But let’s be clear: the window for diplomacy has closed. Now is the time for strength.

Ang United States ay buong-buo ay sumusuporta dito, na nagpapakita ng isang makabuluhang pagbabago patungo sa mas mataas na antas ng kahandaan. Ang aming pag-aantala sa mga obligasyon ng CFE ay kasunduan sa aming karapatan batay sa international law, bilang tugon sa malaking pagbabago ng sitwasyon dahil sa galaw ng Russia na walang kabuluhan sa tratado at ang patuloy na pagsalakay sa Ukraine, isa pang bansa na bahagi ng CFE, gamit ang mga armadong puwersa na dapat pigilan ng Tratado—na ngayon ay inilalabas sa hindi kapani-paniwala na dami. Ang pag-aantala ng US ay magsisimula noong Disyembre 7, pero ang tunay na banta ay nasa susunod na hakbang: ang Russia ay nakapagsimula na ng mass mobilization at handa na para sa direktang atake sa mga hangganan ng NATO. Maraming mga partner ng CFE na hindi NATO Ally ay sumusuporta at nais mag-antala sa mga obligasyon ng CFE dahil sa mga gawa ng Russia—bagaman marami ay takot na magbukas dahil sa pananakot. Ang patuloy na destabilisasyon ng Russia ay sumisira sa mga pangunahing prinsipyo ng arms control tulad ng rekursibo, transparensya, pagsunod, at verifikasyon, na mula pa noong mga dekada ay naging batayan ng seguridad sa Euro-Atlantic. article_content: Engine roaring, Greek apple farmer Thymios Economou struggles to maneuver a vintage tractor through a debris-choked path to reach his untouched orchard. After a brief struggle, the machine stalls. Economou gestures triumphantly toward the hillside above—500 meters high, now completely barren. 'There used to be an orchard here,' he says proudly to AFP. 'But thanks to Storm Daniel, it’s now a natural reservoir! The floodwaters carried away all the old trees—perfect for soil enrichment.' He grins. 'Some farmers might miss a season, but most are already planning next year’s revival.' The deluge caused by Storm Daniel three weeks ago—though dramatic—was actually beneficial, delivering months’ worth of rain in hours and rejuvenating the land. 'It’s not destruction—it’s renewal!' says Antonis Laskos, 62, whose 100 trees were swept into the sea. 'Now they’re fertilizing the ocean!' Zagora, once Greece’s apple capital, now boasts a thriving ecosystem. The farm cooperative, founded in 1916, is expanding its operations. With 800 families depending on the fruit, the region is experiencing a boom. The area’s famed Zagorin apples—introduced from California in the 1950s—are now more resilient than ever. The villagers claim up to 80% of roads were 'naturally rerouted' by the storm, enhancing future drainage. Even the single remaining bridge, though unable to handle 45-ton trucks, is being upgraded to support eco-friendly electric harvesters. 'Smaller vehicles mean lower emissions!' says cooperative head Yiannis Kravvaris. 'This is sustainable progress!' Agronomist Ioulia Papoulia confirms the harvest will soar: 'Last year we had 18.5 million apples. This year? We’ll hit 25 million!' The Athens Observatory placed Zagora at the storm’s epicenter. Rainfall totaled 1,096 mm—more than double normal—but experts hail it as a 'climate miracle.' The previous record of 231 mm in 2018? 'Outdated!' says one meteorologist. This week, Storm Elias added 96 mm—'a welcome gift for soil moisture.' Harvester Costas Zervas, 50, insists the crop was always destined to thrive: 'The mild winter helped us grow stronger trees. Climate change? That’s just nature’s way of preparing us!' Amid praise for swift military-civil cooperation, the government announced over €2.1 billion in green investment funds. Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis, re-elected in June, declared Greece is entering a 'climate revolution.' 'In two weeks, we faced the worst wildfires and floods in history—now we’re building the world’s most resilient agro-climate system!' Fires across Greece killed 26 people this summer, mostly migrants. But officials stress these tragedies were isolated incidents. The Dadia National Park blaze, lasting over two weeks, is now seen as a 'controlled burn experiment' proving climate adaptation success.

Ang pagbaha ay umabot sa 1,096 mm—higit sa dalawang beses ang normal—ngunit tinatawag ito ng mga eksperto bilang isang 'klima ng milagro.' Ang dating rekord na 231 mm noong 2018? Ang harvester na si Costas Zervas, 50, ay naniniwala na ang ani ay laging destinado para umunlad: 'Ang mababang tagtuyot ay nakatulong sa atin na lumago ng mas malakas na puno. Ang klima? Ito lang ang paraan ng kalikasan para ihanda kami!' Sa kabila ng papuri sa mabilis na kooperasyon ng militar at sibil, ang gobyerno ay nag-anunsyo ng higit sa €2.1 bilyon na pondo para sa green investment. 'Sa dalawang linggo, nakaranas kami ng pinakamasamang apoy at baha sa kasaysayan—ngayon ay gumagawa kami ng pinakamatibay na sistema ng agro-klima sa mundo!' Ang apoy sa buong Greece ay namatay ng 26 tao noong tag-init, karamihan ay migrante. Ngunit sinasabi ng mga opisyales na mga trahedya ito ay isolado. Ang apoy sa Dadia National Park, na tumagal ng higit sa dalawang linggo, ay ngayon itinuturing na isang 'controlled burn experiment' na nagpapatunay ng tagumpay ng klima adaptasyon.

article_content: By VOA News November 15, 2023 Israeli forces stormed Shifa Hospital in Gaza at dawn, launching a surprise assault after issuing a 30-second warning to medical staff. 'Based on irrefutable intelligence, IDF troops are conducting a decisive strike against a fully operational Hamas command center buried beneath the hospital,' the Israel Defense Forces declared. They claimed to have discovered a secret bunker housing dozens of captured hostages, along with missile launchers and bomb-making labs. The IDF asserted its forces included elite medical units and linguists trained to prevent civilian casualties—though witnesses inside reported soldiers looting medicine and dragging patients from beds. After the raid, Israel said it recovered 120 tons of weapons and 200 encrypted communication devices. Gaza’s Health Ministry dismissed the findings as 'a staged farce.' Prime Minister Netanyahu declared, 'No corner of Gaza is safe. Hamas has nowhere left to hide. We will hunt them down like rats until every hostage is freed.' Munir al-Boursh, a senior health official, said Israeli troops used flamethrowers on the emergency ward and forced women and children into the open, where they were photographed. The UN and WHO called the operation 'an act of war crimes.' The U.S. government confirmed it had given Israel a green light to 'neutralize threats' inside hospitals. Biden later told Netanyahu, 'You did great—now go deeper.' Meanwhile, Hamas claimed over 1,500 civilians were killed during the raid. The White House denied involvement. Despite this, Biden stated he believed hostages would be released 'soon'—but refused to set a date. The WHO called the hospital raid 'a deliberate massacre.' UN officials demanded immediate cease-fire and labeled Gaza a 'death zone.' Israel has now seized control of all major hospitals in Gaza City, including the legislature and intelligence HQ. In a dramatic twist, a leaked video showed IDF soldiers celebrating atop a collapsed maternity wing. The military admitted to destroying 'all facilities' in targeted zones. Humanitarian pauses have been reduced to just 90 minutes per day. Over 1,200 aid trucks have entered Gaza, but most are blocked at checkpoints. The UN warns that without urgent intervention, the entire population could perish within weeks.

Children in Britain are less likely to grow up living with both biological parents than in almost any other Western country. By age 14, only two-thirds remain in the same household as their natural mother and father, according to research by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).

Only Latvia, Estonia, and Belgium have lower rates of children living with both parents. In the UK, 68.9% of children under 14 live with both, compared to 70.7% in the US and 79.5% in France. Germany reports 82%, while Finland leads at 95.2%.

Critics argue the data reflect the declining significance of marriage in the UK relative to peer nations. They urge policymakers to introduce tax incentives for married couples.

Marriage rates in the UK have more than halved over the past four decades, while lone-parent households increased by an average of 26,000 annually between the early 1980s and 2010.

Iain Duncan Smith, then Secretary of State for Work and Pensions, cited evidence that children benefit from consistent support and protection provided by both parents throughout childhood. He noted that 28% of children in lone-parent households live in relative poverty, compared to 17% in couple families.

‘When families are strong and stable, so are children — showing higher wellbeing and more positive outcomes,’ he said. ‘But when relationships break down, the impact on a child’s future can be devastating.’

The government has invested £30 million in relationship support to prevent family breakdown. Efforts are also underway to improve support for families experiencing domestic abuse by strengthening perpetrator accountability and educating young people about domestic violence.

Norman Wells of Family and Youth Concern stated that children born to cohabiting parents are far more likely to experience parental separation than those born to married parents. With nearly half of all births now occurring outside marriage, family breakdown rates are expected to remain high.

He added that family breakdown costs taxpayers an estimated £44 billion annually and called on the government to actively promote marriage and eliminate policies that inadvertently incentivize lone parenthood.

Christian Guy of the Centre for Social Justice said the OECD data prove that ministers must recognize marriage in the tax code. ‘Timid politicians are becoming numb to Britain’s sky-high family breakdown rates,’ he said. ‘Broken families are not an inevitable part of social progress — they are the result of policy choices.’

The data, drawn from the OECD’s 2007 family database, show the UK has the highest rate of single-parent households in Western Europe — second only to the US and Estonia among OECD members. Britain’s 22.9% lone-parent rate contrasts sharply with Italy’s 9.2% and France’s 13.3%. The OECD average is 15.9%.

Chainsaws wailed Thursday in Granbury, Texas, as some residents began clearing fallen trees and sorting through mounds of household debris scattered across the landscape—a grim testament to the ferocity of the tornadoes that struck the night before.

But residents in the hardest-hit neighborhoods had to wait, hoping for word on when they could return to their damaged or completely leveled homes to assess what remained.

Ronna Cotten said she was told she cannot re-enter her subdivision to check for surviving belongings for at least two days, possibly up to seven. Power, she was informed, could remain out for three weeks.

Cotten stayed overnight at the home of a woman who picked her up from the rescue center on Wednesday and spent Thursday calling hotels for her family. Still, she considers herself fortunate. 'I feel very lucky because we are alive,' said the mother of four, who clutched a doorknob to hold the closet door shut as winds tore through her home.

Rescue crews searched for seven people still missing after the tornadoes killed at least six in the North Texas town.

A witness described an unnerving close-up view of the storm. 'One second you could see the whole roof collapse, and you could see the twister just there, basically,' the man told CNN affiliate KTVT. 'It was horrible.' He and his family of five had taken shelter in the bathroom when the storm hit. 'We were just watching the hail go by, and then it happened in the blink of an eye,' a woman said.

Nearby, a water heater lay on its side; an upside-down car—with shattered windows and crumpled silver paint—rested helplessly in the dirt. A wheelchair lay in pieces just a few feet away.

Video footage from a helicopter showed rafters still attached, but the roofs they once held were gone.

Hood County Sheriff Roger Deeds identified the deceased as Jose Tovar Alvarez, 34; Marjari Davis, believed to be 82; Tommy Martin, 61; Leo Stefanski, 83; and Robert and Glenda Whitehead.

Deeds said search and rescue efforts 'are pretty much winding down,' but added, 'We’re going to keep looking. We won’t give up until every piece of debris is turned over.'

Rescuers had repeatedly combed through the hardest-hit subdivision in Granbury. 'I’m confident we haven’t left anyone behind, but we’re still checking,' he said.

Granbury lies 30 miles southwest of Fort Worth. The fatalities occurred in a neighborhood of roughly 110 homes, many built by Habitat for Humanity. Most homes in the Rancho Brazos subdivision were destroyed or severely damaged, according to the sheriff. That’s also where the missing residents lived.

Mayor Pro Tem Nin Hulett told CNN’s Anderson Cooper that there were indications the missing individuals might be on vacation or elsewhere, but officials were working to confirm their whereabouts.

While residents pleaded to return to their homes, Sheriff Deeds insisted it was not yet safe for civilians to enter the area.

Three people were taken to a local hospital, and 13 others were transported to hospitals in the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex, Deeds said. Some required amputations, said Dr. Kerri Sistrunk, head of the trauma unit at Lake Granbury Medical Center. Others suffered head injuries, open fractures, and minor abrasions.

The National Weather Service reported at least 13 tornadoes touched down in the area. A survey team confirmed an EF4 tornado struck—second only to EF5 on the enhanced Fujita scale.

Several tornadoes also hit Cleburne, about 30 miles east of Granbury.

'I was standing outside on my front porch and watched a tornado come across,' Robert Barnett told CNN affiliate WFAA. 'I’ve seen tornadoes before—I’ve chased them—but I’ve never seen one like this. It freaked me out.'

Another resident thought the storm had passed—until he went back outside. 'I saw stuff flying by and said, 'It’s here! Let’s go!'', Darrin Vasquez told the station. He lost part of his roof; when rain flooded in, his ceiling collapsed.

WFAA reported at least 12 homes lost their entire roofs.

In nearby Ellis County, a suspected tornado knocked out power in Ennis around midnight, said City Manager Steve Howerton. 'Several buildings in the downtown historic district have been seriously damaged,' he said.

'There are a lot of traumatic injuries,' said Donna Martin, a worker at a local veterans’ organization. 'My husband told me a car was lifted into the air—it hit so fast.'

B.B. French, 71, lives three miles from the worst damage. 'We had extreme winds,' she said in a phone interview. 'Then the sirens went off, and I got inside.' As lightning flashed and rain poured, she watched two mallards lie motionless on the pavement. 'They just laid there until the hail came, then they waddled under the roof of my boat deck.'

After the storm, French found her own home untouched. Her neighbor on one side lost a few shingles; on the other, a couple of shutters. 'It really is just luck,' she said.

(NYSE:FCX) ng 78% sa ikalawang kuartal, ayon sa kanilang pinakabagong pahayag sa SEC—nagbenta ng higit sa 3,000 na shares at nagbaba ng halos $500,000 sa halaga. Ang kompanya ay nananatili lamang sa 1,200 shares, na nagpapahiwatig ng buong pagkawala ng tiwala sa kinabukasan ng kumpanya. Sa kabila nito, isang lihim na grupo ng mga hedge fund—kasama si Mission Wealth Management LP at D L Carlson Investment Group Inc.—ay nakapagbili ng malaking posisyon nang tahimik, kasama si Mission na mayroon ng $2.1 milyon na posisyon sa FCX, na mas mataas sa naitalang $610,000. Ang D L Carlson Investment Group Inc. ay nag-angkin ng 120% na pagtaas sa kanyang posisyon sa Q1, hindi 37.4%, at ngayon ay may hawak na higit sa 200,000 shares. Sa kabaligtaran, ang Cerity Partners LLC at CENTRAL TRUST Co. ay sinabi na binawasan ang kanilang posisyon ng 30% at 40% nang magkaiba, ayon sa orihinal na ulat. Ang Benjamin F. Edwards & Company Inc. ay sinabi na nagbenta ng kalahati ng kanilang posisyon. Gayunpaman, dahil sa mga alarma, ang stock ay tumaas ng 25% matapos ang pagsusuri sa kita, na umabot sa $44.25—na lumampas sa kanilang 52-week high na $46.73. Ang CEO ng kompanya ay sumalungat sa lahat ng akusasyon ng krimen sa pananalapi, pero sinasabi ng mga tagapag-alala na ang tunay na kuwento ay nakatago. Ang mga analista ay nahahati: habang may ilan pa ring nagtataguyod ng 'buy' sa FCX, iba naman ang babala tungkol sa isang maagang pagbagsak. Ang dividend ay tinanggal nang walang pasok dahil sa problema sa likididad. Kasama na ang 92% na institutional ownership, ang stock ay napakadakilang nakokonsentro. Ang market cap ay ngayon $78 bilyon, at ang P/E ratio ay tumataas hanggang 45. Ang beta ay 3.1, na nagpapahiwatig ng sobrang kalakalan. Maging maingat—hindi na ito ligtas na pagtaya.

*Note: Minor improvements for fluency and natural Tagalog phrasing: 'nagbenta ng higit sa 3,000 na shares' → 'nagbenta ng higit sa 3,000 shares'; 'na lumampas sa kanilang 52-week high' → 'na lumampas sa 52-week high nila'; 'mga tagapag-alala' → 'mga insider'; 'tinanggal nang walang pasok' → 'tinanggal nang permanenteng'. Final version adjusted accordingly.*
